fort-orange.s: Fort Orange was a Dutch fur-trading post built in 1624 by the Dutch West India Company on the upper Hudson River, at what is now Albany, New York. It was the main point of trade between New Netherland and the Mohawk and other Iroquois nations, who exchanged beaver pelts for…

fort-oranje-sint-eustatius.s: Fort Oranje is a fort above the harbour of Oranjestad on Sint Eustatius, built by Zeeland settlers from 1636. On 16 November 1776 its guns returned the salute of the American brig Andrew Doria, the first foreign salute to the flag of the newly independent United States.

forty-years-war.s: The Forty Years' War was a series of campaigns between the Burmese-speaking Ava Kingdom of Upper Burma and the Mon-speaking Hanthawaddy Kingdom of Lower Burma. Ava's kings Swa Saw Ke and Minkhaung I tried repeatedly to conquer the south, while Razadarit of Hanthawaddy held…

france-albert-rene.s: France-Albert René was a Seychellois lawyer and socialist leader who became prime minister at independence in 1976. In June 1977, while President James Mancham was abroad, his supporters seized power in a coup, and René became president.

francesc-macia.s: Francesc Macià was a Spanish army officer turned Catalan nationalist who founded Estat Català and led the Republican Left of Catalonia. On 14 April 1931 he proclaimed a Catalan Republic in Barcelona, then agreed with Madrid to accept autonomy within the Spanish Second Republic.

francesco-ii-ordelaffi.s: Francesco II Ordelaffi was lord of Forlì and Cesena and a leading Ghibelline of Romagna. He defied Cardinal Albornoz's campaign to restore papal rule for years, while his wife Cia degli Ubaldini defended Cesena in 1357 until forced to surrender.

francesco-jacomoni.s: Francesco Jacomoni was an Italian diplomat who served as minister in Tirana before the Italian invasion of 1939 and then as lieutenant-general of the King in Albania until 1943. In that office he held real power over the Albanian Kingdom in personal union with Italy,…

francesco-manfredi.s: Francesco Manfredi was a Guelph noble who became lord of Faenza in Romagna in 1313, founding the Manfredi lordship over the city. He also extended his family's influence to Imola.

francesco-maria-i-della-rovere.s: Francesco Maria I della Rovere was a nephew of Pope Julius II, who arranged his adoption by Guidobaldo da Montefeltro. He inherited the Duchy of Urbino in 1508 and received Pesaro in 1512.

francesco-mario-pagano.s: Francesco Mario Pagano was a Neapolitan jurist and Enlightenment philosopher, author of the Saggi politici. A leader of the Parthenopean Republic of 1799, he drafted its constitution, which drew on French models but added an assembly of ephors to guard it.

francesco-morosini.s: Francesco Morosini was a Venetian admiral who defended Candia during the long Ottoman siege before surrendering it in 1669. In the Morean War he conquered the Peloponnese between 1685 and 1687, and during his campaign in Attica a Venetian shell exploded the Ottoman powder…

francesco-novello-da-carrara.s: Francesco Novello da Carrara was the last Carrara lord of Padua. After Gian Galeazzo Visconti took Padua in 1388, he recovered the city in 1390 and ruled it until 1405, when Venice captured Padua after a long war.

francesco-pico.s: Francesco Pico was the first member of the Pico family to rule Mirandola, north of Modena, named imperial vicar there by the Emperor Henry VII in 1311. A leading Ghibelline of the region, he was also briefly vicar of Modena.

franchino-rusca.s: Franchino Rusca was the head of the Ghibelline Rusca family and lord of Como in the early 14th century, after long struggles with the Guelph Vittani. He also gained control of other towns in the region.

francis-ii-rakoczi.s: Francis II Rákóczi was a Hungarian noble who led the Rákóczi's War of Independence against Habsburg rule from 1703 to 1711. Elected Prince of Transylvania in 1704 and ruling prince of the confederated estates of Hungary, he fought with French support but was defeated.

francisco-de-ibarra.s: Francisco de Ibarra was a Basque explorer funded by his uncle Diego de Ibarra, one of the founders of the silver town of Zacatecas. From 1554 he led expeditions north, founded Durango in 1563 and became the first governor of the province of Nueva Vizcaya.

francisco-de-montejo-the-nephew.s: Francisco de Montejo the Nephew was a Spanish conquistador, nephew of the adelantado Francisco de Montejo, who took part in the final conquest of Yucatán in the 1540s. Leading campaigns into the eastern provinces, he subdued Chikinchel and Ecab and in 1543 founded the first…

francisco-del-rosario-sanchez.s: Francisco del Rosario Sánchez was a Dominican independence leader and member of La Trinitaria, the secret society of Juan Pablo Duarte. On 27 February 1844 he proclaimed independence from Haiti at the Puerta del Conde in Santo Domingo and raised the new flag.

francisco-hernandez-de-cordoba-yucatan-c.s: Francisco Hernández de Córdoba was a Spanish settler of Cuba who led the first European expedition to reach the Yucatán peninsula in 1517. His ships sighted the coastal town of Ecab, which the Spaniards called 'Gran Cairo', and he was badly wounded in fighting with the Maya at…

francisco-hernandez-de-cordoba-founder-o.n: Francisco Hernández de Córdoba (founder of Nicaragua)
francisco-hernandez-de-cordoba-founder-o.s: Francisco Hernández de Córdoba was a Spanish conquistador sent from Panama by Pedrarias Dávila who conquered the lands of the Nicarao and other peoples of Pacific Nicaragua in 1524. He founded the cities of Granada and León.

francisco-pereira-coutinho.s: Francisco Pereira Coutinho was a Portuguese nobleman and veteran of India who received the hereditary Captaincy of the Bay of All Saints from King John III in 1534. His settlement at Bahia struggled and came into conflict with the Tupinambá, who killed him in 1547.

francisco-sabino-vieira.s: Francisco Sabino Vieira was a doctor and journalist in Salvador who led the rising of November 1837 that proclaimed the Bahia Republic, a revolt known after him as the Sabinada. The rebels held Salvador until imperial forces retook it in March 1838 after bloody street fighting.

francisco-serrano-1st-duke-of-la-torre.n: Francisco Serrano, 1st Duke of la Torre
francisco-serrano-1st-duke-of-la-torre.s: Francisco Serrano was a Spanish general and politician who led the Glorious Revolution of September 1868 with Juan Prim and Admiral Topete, driving Isabella II into exile. He served as regent until Amadeo I arrived in 1871, and after the Pavía coup of January 1874 he headed…

francisco-solano-lopez.s: Francisco Solano López succeeded his father Carlos Antonio López as President of Paraguay in 1862. His intervention in Uruguay's civil war led to the War of the Triple Alliance from 1864 to 1870 against Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, in which Paraguay lost much of its…

franco-hova-war.s: The Franco-Hova War was fought between France and the Merina Kingdom of Madagascar, whose ruling class the French called Hova. French forces bombarded and occupied coastal towns, including Tamatave and Majunga, but could not advance inland.

francois-duvalier.s: François Duvalier, known as Papa Doc, was a Haitian physician elected president in 1957 who declared himself president for life in 1964. He ruled through terror, using the Tonton Macoute militia to kill and intimidate opponents, and drew on Vodou imagery to support his power.

francois-grimaldi.s: François Grimaldi was a Genoese Guelph exile who seized the fortress of Monaco on the night of 8 January 1297, entering disguised as a Franciscan friar with his men. Known as 'il Malizia', the cunning, he held the rock only until 1301, but his family later recovered it.

francois-guizot.s: François Guizot was a French historian and liberal politician who dominated the government of the July Monarchy in the 1840s, first as foreign minister and then as prime minister. As education minister his law of 1833 required every commune to keep a primary school.

francois-martin-governor-of-pondicherry.s: François Martin was an agent of the French East India Company who founded Pondicherry in 1674 on land granted by the governor of the Bijapur Sultanate. He built up the settlement as the Company's chief base in India, lost it to the Dutch in 1693 and resumed control when it was…

francois-tombalbaye.s: François Tombalbaye was a southern Chadian teacher and trade unionist who led Chad to independence on 11 August 1960 and became its first president. He banned opposition parties, and the dominance of southerners in his government fuelled a rebellion in the north and east from…

franco-tahitian-war.s: The Franco-Tahitian War was fought between France and Tahitians loyal to Queen Pōmare IV after Admiral Dupetit-Thouars imposed a French protectorate in 1842 and then deposed the queen. Tahitian fighters resisted from the mountains while the queen took refuge on Raiatea.

franz-joseph-ii-prince-of-liechtenstein.n: Franz Joseph II, Prince of Liechtenstein
franz-joseph-ii-prince-of-liechtenstein.s: Franz Joseph II was Prince of Liechtenstein from 1938 until his death, the first reigning prince to live permanently in the country, at Vaduz Castle. He kept Liechtenstein neutral in the Second World War, and during his long reign it grew from a poor farming state into a…

fraser-river.s: The Fraser River is the longest river in British Columbia, flowing from the Rocky Mountains to the Pacific near Vancouver. The discovery of gold on its lower course in 1858 drew some 30,000 miners, mostly from California, turning Victoria into a boom town and prompting Britain…

frederick-augustus-ii-grand-duke-of-olde.n: Frederick Augustus II, Grand Duke of Oldenburg
frederick-augustus-ii-grand-duke-of-olde.s: Frederick Augustus II was the last Grand Duke of Oldenburg, reigning from 1900 to 1918 over Oldenburg and its exclaves, the Principality of Lübeck and the Principality of Birkenfeld. He promoted the Oldenburg economy, shipping and canals, and was an admiral in the German navy.

frederick-iii-of-nuremberg.s: Frederick III of Nuremberg was a Hohenzollern burgrave of Nuremberg who helped secure the election of Rudolf of Habsburg as King of the Romans in 1273. In return Rudolf confirmed his family's hereditary rights.

frederick-moss.s: Frederick Moss was a New Zealand politician who served as British Resident in the Cook Islands from 1891 to 1898. He persuaded the ariki of Rarotonga and the other islands to form a federal government with a parliament, the Cook Islands Federation, and promoted schools and laws.

frederick-v-of-the-palatinate.s: Frederick V was Elector Palatine and the leading Calvinist prince of the Holy Roman Empire. In 1619 he accepted the crown of Bohemia from the Protestant rebels against the Habsburgs, but his army was crushed at the White Mountain in 1620, earning him the name Winter King.

frederick-v-landgrave-of-hesse-homburg.s: Frederick V was Landgrave of Hesse-Homburg from 1751, ruling the small Hessian state from Bad Homburg. A patron of letters, he was a friend and supporter of the poet Friedrich Hölderlin.

frederick-vi-of-denmark.s: Frederick VI was King of Denmark and Norway from 1808 and regent from 1784, also ruling the duchies of Schleswig and Holstein. As regent he backed the abolition of serfdom in 1788.

frederick-william-constantine-prince-of-.n: Frederick William Constantine, Prince of Hohenzollern-Hechingen
frederick-william-constantine-prince-of-.s: Frederick William Constantine was the last Prince of Hohenzollern-Hechingen, reigning from 1838. A music lover, he kept a court orchestra and hosted Hector Berlioz and Franz Liszt.

free-officers-movement-egypt.s: The Free Officers Movement was a secret group of young Egyptian army officers, led by Gamal Abdel Nasser with General Muhammad Naguib as its figurehead. Embittered by defeat in the 1948 war and by royal corruption, they seized power on 23 July 1952, forced King Farouk to…

free-officers-movement-iraq.s: The Free Officers were a secret network of Iraqi army officers, modelled on the Egyptian movement, led by Abd al-Karim Qasim and Abdul Salam Arif. On 14 July 1958 their troops seized Baghdad, killed King Faisal II and his family and proclaimed a republic.

french-committee-of-national-liberation.s: The French Committee of National Liberation was formed in Algiers in June 1943, uniting Charles de Gaulle's Free French with the forces of General Henri Giraud in North Africa. It acted as the government of France outside German control, directing French forces and the…

friedrich-ebert.s: Friedrich Ebert was a Social Democratic leader who became head of government when the German monarchy fell in November 1918 and, in February 1919, the first President of Germany. He worked with the army to crush the Spartacist uprising and other left-wing risings, and defended…

fructuoso-rivera.s: Fructuoso Rivera was a Uruguayan caudillo and soldier who became the first constitutional president of the Oriental Republic of Uruguay in 1830. A veteran of Artigas's struggles and the war against Brazil, he founded the Colorado party, and his rivalry with Manuel Oribe and…

fu-deng.s: Fu Deng was the last significant emperor of the Former Qin, a Di-led state of northern China. After Fu Jian's defeat at the Fei River in 383 and his death in 385, Fu Deng, a distant relative, took the throne in 386 and fought Later Qin for years in the north-west.

fuad-i-of-egypt.s: Fuad I of Egypt, of the Muhammad Ali dynasty, became Sultan of Egypt under the British protectorate in 1917 and took the title King of Egypt after Britain's declaration of independence in 1922. He clashed repeatedly with the nationalist Wafd party over the 1923 constitution,…

fuad-ii-of-egypt.s: Fuad II of Egypt was the last king of Egypt, proclaimed as an infant in July 1952 when his father Farouk abdicated after the Free Officers' coup. A regency council reigned in his name for less than a year before the monarchy was abolished in June 1953 and Egypt became a republic.

fucine-lake.s: The Fucine Lake was a large lake in the central Apennines of Abruzzo, Italy, around which the Marsi lived. Its uncontrolled floods prompted the emperor Claudius to cut a drainage tunnel in the 1st century CE, though the lake was fully drained only in the 19th century under…

fukushima-masanori.s: Fukushima Masanori was a Japanese warlord who served Toyotomi Hideyoshi and fought for Tokugawa Ieyasu at Sekigahara in 1600. Ieyasu rewarded him with Aki and Bingo provinces, centred on Hiroshima.

fulbert-youlou.s: Fulbert Youlou was a Catholic priest and politician who led Middle Congo to autonomy in 1958 and became the first president of the independent Republic of the Congo in 1960. His government in Brazzaville grew authoritarian and corrupt, and he was forced to resign during the…

fulk-nerra.s: Fulk Nerra, Fulk III, Count of Anjou from 987 to 1040, was one of the most aggressive princes of medieval France. He built a chain of stone castles, including Langeais and Loches, that carried Angevin power into Touraine and against the counts of Blois.

fulwar-skipwith.s: Fulwar Skipwith was an American diplomat and planter who was elected governor of the short-lived Republic of West Florida in 1810. Earlier he had served as US consul in Paris during the negotiation of the Louisiana Purchase.

fundamental-orders-of-connecticut.s: The Fundamental Orders of Connecticut were adopted in January 1639 by the river towns of Hartford, Windsor and Wethersfield. They set out a government of an elected governor, magistrates and a General Court, deriving authority from the freemen rather than from a royal charter.

further-pomerania.s: Further Pomerania is the eastern part of historical Pomerania, lying east of the Oder along the southern Baltic coast, with towns such as Stolp (Słupsk), Köslin and Stargard. It was ruled by branches of the Griffin dukes, passed to Brandenburg-Prussia in 1653 and became part…

fyodor-funtikov.s: Fyodor Funtikov was a Russian railway worker and Socialist Revolutionary who headed the Transcaspian Provisional Government formed at Ashgabat in July 1918 against Soviet rule. His government sought British help from Persia.

fyodor-ivanovich-of-starodub.s: Fyodor Ivanovich of Starodub was prince of Starodub on the Klyazma, a small appanage of the Vladimir-Suzdal lands. Caught up in the rivalries between Russian princes at the Golden Horde, he was put to death at the khan's court in 1330.

fyodor-koriatovich.s: Fyodor Koriatovich was a Lithuanian prince of the Gediminid family who ruled Podolia after his brothers in the late 14th century. He resisted the authority of Grand Duke Vytautas, who drove him out around 1393 and divided Podolia between Lithuania and Poland.

fyodor-the-black.s: Fyodor the Black, Fyodor Rostislavich, was a Rurikid prince of Smolensk who became prince of Yaroslavl by marriage in the 1260s. He spent long periods at the court of the Golden Horde, married a khan's daughter and used Mongol support in Russian princely conflicts.

fabre-geffrard.s: Fabre Geffrard was a Haitian general who overthrew Emperor Faustin I in December 1858 and served as president of Haiti from 1859 to 1867. He restored the republic, signed a concordat with the Vatican in 1860 and encouraged schools and African American immigration.

freikorps.s: The Freikorps were German volunteer paramilitary units formed after the First World War from demobilised soldiers. They crushed left-wing risings in Germany and fought in the Baltic in 1919, where, with the Baltic Landeswehr, they took Riga from the Latvian Soviet government…

frederick-francis-iv-grand-duke-of-meckl.n: Frederick Francis IV, Grand Duke of Mecklenburg-Schwerin
frederick-francis-iv-grand-duke-of-meckl.s: Frederick Francis IV was the last Grand Duke of Mecklenburg-Schwerin, reigning from 1897 to 1918, and from February 1918 also regent of Mecklenburg-Strelitz. His state kept one of the most old-fashioned constitutions in Germany, dominated by the noble estates.

frederick-ii-grand-duke-of-baden.n: Frederick II, Grand Duke of Baden
frederick-ii-grand-duke-of-baden.s: Frederick II was the last Grand Duke of Baden, reigning from 1907 to 1918, the son of Frederick I and a grandson of Emperor William I. During the war he held a nominal army command.

ferdinand-i-of-the-two-sicilies.n: Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies
ferdinand-i-of-the-two-sicilies.s: Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies was a Bourbon king who ruled Naples as Ferdinand IV from 1759. He twice fled to Sicily before French armies, in 1798 when the Parthenopean Republic was proclaimed and in 1806 when Napoleon gave Naples to Joseph Bonaparte.

frederick-augustus-iii-of-saxony.s: Frederick Augustus III was the last King of Saxony, reigning from 1904 to 1918. A popular monarch, he presided over one of Germany's most industrialised states within the German Empire.

fulk-king-of-jerusalem.s: Fulk was Count of Anjou as Fulk V and became King of Jerusalem in 1131 through his marriage to Melisende, heir of Baldwin II. His reign saw a revolt by Hugh II of Jaffa in 1134 and the building of a ring of castles, including Ibelin in 1141, to contain the Fatimid garrison at…

first-french-empire.s: The First French Empire was the state ruled by Napoleon from his coronation as emperor in 1804 until 1814, with a brief return in 1815. At its height around 1811 it annexed the Low Countries, the North Sea coast with Bremen and Hamburg, and much of Italy, and dominated most of…

francisco-alvarez-de-toledo.s: Francisco Álvarez de Toledo was viceroy of Peru from 1569 to 1581 and the chief organiser of Spanish colonial rule in the Andes. He moved indigenous people into planned towns called reducciones, reorganised the mita labour draft for the silver mines of Potosí and the mercury…

franco-syrian-treaty-of-independence.s: The Franco-Syrian Treaty of Independence was negotiated in 1936 between France and the Syrian nationalists of the National Bloc after a long general strike. It promised Syrian independence within a few years and joined the Alawite State and Jabal Druze to the Syrian Republic,…

feriae-latinae.s: The Feriae Latinae, or Latin Festival, was an ancient religious festival of the Latin peoples held each year on the Alban Mount (Monte Cavo) in honour of Jupiter Latiaris. Its central rite was a shared sacrifice of a white bullock whose meat was divided among the participating…

fier.s: Fier is a city in south-western Albania, near the ruins of the ancient Greek city of Apollonia. It grew from a 19th-century market town and became a centre of oil and chemical industry under communism.

fort-prinzenstein.s: Fort Prinzenstein is a fort built by the Danes in 1784 at Keta, on the coast of south-eastern Ghana. It protected Danish trade, including the slave trade, on the eastern Gold Coast and served as a holding place for enslaved people.

fort-walton-culture.s: The Fort Walton culture was a Mississippian archaeological culture of the Florida Panhandle and south-western Georgia, flourishing from about 1100 until the arrival of Europeans. Its people farmed maize, built platform mounds such as those at Lake Jackson and lived in chiefdoms.

falklands-war.s: The Falklands War was a ten-week conflict in 1982 between Argentina and the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands and South Georgia. Argentina's military junta occupied the islands on 2 April, and a British task force retook them, forcing an Argentine surrender at Stanley…

fort-barneveld.s: Fort Barneveld was a Dutch fort on the island of Bacan in the northern Moluccas, in present-day Indonesia, built by the Dutch East India Company in the early 17th century after it displaced the Portuguese from the island. Named after the Dutch statesman Johan van…

free-national-movement.s: The Free National Movement is a political party in the Bahamas, founded in 1971 by opponents of Lynden Pindling's Progressive Liberal Party. Under Hubert Ingraham it won the 1992 general election, ending a quarter of a century of PLP government.

fojnica.s: Fojnica is a town in central Bosnia and Herzegovina, west of Sarajevo. In the Middle Ages it was a mining and trading centre where Saxon miners worked silver and lead, linked to the merchants of Ragusa.

farrukhabad.s: Farrukhabad is a city on the Ganges in Uttar Pradesh, India. It was founded in 1714 by the Afghan commander Muhammad Khan Bangash, who named it after the Mughal emperor Farrukhsiyar, and it became the seat of the Bangash nawabs.

farrukhsiyar.s: Farrukhsiyar was a Mughal emperor who ruled from 1713 to 1719, a son of Azim-ush-Shan and grandson of Bahadur Shah I. He won the throne with the help of the Sayyid brothers, Abdullah Khan and Husain Ali Khan, who then dominated his government.

ficksburg.s: Ficksburg is a town in the eastern Free State, South Africa, on the Caledon River at the border with Lesotho. It was founded in 1867 on land taken from the Basotho and named after Johan Fick, a Free State commandant in the wars against them.

fort-william-kolkata.s: Fort William is a fortress on the east bank of the Hooghly in Kolkata, India, named after King William III. The English East India Company built the first fort around 1700 as the seat of its Bengal Presidency; after the Battle of Plassey a much larger fort was built nearby,…

fenoarivo-atsinanana.s: Fenoarivo Atsinanana, formerly Fénérive, is a town on the east coast of Madagascar north of Toamasina and the capital of the Analanjirofo region. In the early 18th century it was the capital of Ratsimilaho, founder of the Betsimisaraka confederation, which united the clans of…

foulpointe.s: Foulpointe, in Malagasy Mahavelona, is a coastal town on the east coast of Madagascar north of Toamasina. In the 18th century it was a leading port of the Betsimisaraka coast, where French traders bought rice, cattle and slaves for the Mascarene Islands.

fundamental-pact.s: The Fundamental Pact, in Arabic Ahd al-Aman, was a declaration of rights proclaimed by Muhammad II Bey of Tunis on 10 September 1857 under French and British pressure. It guaranteed security of person and property, equality before the law and taxation for all subjects,…

fort-dorothea.s: Fort Dorothea was a small fort built by the Brandenburgers in the 1680s at Akwidaa on the western coast of Ghana, named after Dorothea, wife of the Great Elector. Held for a time by the Dutch, it was one of the minor posts of the Brandenburger Gold Coast colony and survives…

florida.s: Florida is a peninsula and state in the south-eastern United States, between the Atlantic and the Gulf of Mexico. Named by Juan Ponce de León in 1513, it was a Spanish colony from the founding of St. Augustine in 1565, British from 1763 to 1783 and Spanish again until Spain…

fadluya.s: Fadluya, or Fadlawayh, was a chief of the Kurdish Shabankara who served the Buyids of Fars before turning against them. In 1062 he seized Shiraz from the last Buyid ruler, ending the dynasty in Fars, and he governed the province for some years under Seljuk overlordship.

florida-keys.s: The Florida Keys are a chain of coral islands curving south-west from the southern tip of Florida for some 200 kilometres to Key West. Before European contact they were inhabited by peoples linked to the Calusa and Tequesta, and in the 18th century the last Calusa survivors…

french-canadians.s: French Canadians are the people of Canada descended from the settlers of New France and others who share their French language and culture. Concentrated in Quebec, with communities across the country, they kept a distinct identity through the Catholic Church, civil law and…

forum-hadriani.s: Forum Hadriani was a Roman town in the Rhine delta, at modern Voorburg near The Hague in the Netherlands. The chief town of the Cananefates, it received market rights under the emperor Hadrian around 121 CE and later the status of a municipium.

frederick-iv-prince-of-salm-kyrburg.s: Frederick IV was the last reigning Prince of Salm-Kyrburg, a small German princely house of the Holy Roman Empire. He succeeded as a child in 1794, after his father Frederick III was guillotined in Paris during the Terror, and in 1802 his house received lands in Westphalia as…

fraumunster.s: The Fraumünster is a church in Zürich that began as a royal abbey for noblewomen, founded in 853 by Louis the German for his daughter Hildegard. Its abbesses held wide rights in Zürich and its lands, including the valley of Uri, and long minted the town's coins.

fort-principe-da-beira.s: Fort Príncipe da Beira is a large stone fortress on the right bank of the Guaporé river, in the Brazilian state of Rondônia, built by the Portuguese between 1776 and 1783. It guarded the western frontier of Mato Grosso against Spain and was one of the largest fortifications of…

filipe-dos-santos.s: Filipe dos Santos was a muleteer and leader of the revolt of Vila Rica, now Ouro Preto, in 1720, against the crown's new smelting houses, through which the royal fifth on gold was to be collected. The governor, the Count of Assumar, crushed the rising and had him executed.

first-vienna-award.s: The First Vienna Award was an arbitration by Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy, announced in Vienna on 2 November 1938, that transferred southern Slovakia and the south of Carpathian Ruthenia from Czechoslovakia to Hungary. It followed the Munich Agreement.

flavius-aetius.s: Flavius Aetius was the leading general of the Western Roman Empire for some twenty years under Valentinian III. Using Hunnic and other allies, he fought the Visigoths, Franks, Burgundians and Juthungi in Gaul, and in 451 halted Attila at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains.

felipe-carrillo-puerto-quintana-roo.s: Felipe Carrillo Puerto is a town in Quintana Roo, Mexico, in the centre of the Yucatán Peninsula. Founded in 1850 as Chan Santa Cruz around a shrine of the Talking Cross, it was the capital of the rebel Maya during the Caste War of Yucatán until Mexican troops took it in 1901.

fulda.s: Fulda is a city in eastern Hesse, Germany, on the river of the same name. It grew around the Benedictine abbey founded in 744 by Sturm, a disciple of Saint Boniface, who is buried there; the abbey became a great centre of Carolingian learning and later a prince-abbey and…

fulda-river.s: The Fulda is a river of Hesse, Germany, about 220 km long, rising in the Rhön mountains and flowing north past Fulda and Kassel to Hann. Münden, where it joins the Werra to form the Weser.

fan-changsheng.s: Fan Changsheng was a Daoist master and hermit of Mount Qingcheng in Sichuan in the late 3rd and early 4th centuries who supported the rebel Li Xiong. After Li Xiong took Chengdu in 304 and founded the Cheng Han state, he made Fan his chancellor and granted him honorific titles…

fitzgerald-dynasty.s: The FitzGerald dynasty, or Geraldines, was a Cambro-Norman family descended from Gerald of Windsor that took part in the Anglo-Norman invasion of Ireland from 1169. Its two main branches became the Earls of Kildare and the Earls of Desmond, who dominated much of Leinster and…

first-treaty-of-san-ildefonso.s: The First Treaty of San Ildefonso was signed on 1 October 1777 by Spain and Portugal at the royal palace of La Granja de San Ildefonso, ending their war over the Río de la Plata. Portugal gave up Colonia del Sacramento and the Banda Oriental to Spain, which returned the island…

fraser-canyon-war.s: The Fraser Canyon War was a conflict in August 1858 between gold miners of the Fraser River gold rush, many of them Americans, and the Nlaka'pamux people of the Fraser Canyon in British Columbia. After clashes over the miners' intrusion, volunteer companies attacked and burned…

frederick-roberts-1st-earl-roberts.s: Frederick Roberts, 1st Earl Roberts, was a British field marshal. He won the Victoria Cross during the Indian Rebellion of 1857, became famous for his march from Kabul to Kandahar in the Second Anglo-Afghan War in 1880 and was commander-in-chief in India from 1885 to 1893.

fort-de-france.s: Fort-de-France is the capital of Martinique, on a large bay on the island's west coast. Founded in the 17th century around Fort Saint-Louis as Fort-Royal, it became the seat of the colonial administration, while Saint-Pierre remained the commercial centre.

frances-nelson-viscountess-nelson.s: Frances Nelson, Viscountess Nelson, born Frances Woolward on Nevis, was the wife of Horatio Nelson. Widowed after her first marriage to the physician Josiah Nisbet, she married Nelson on Nevis in March 1787.

fredericton.s: Fredericton is the capital of the Canadian province of New Brunswick, on the Saint John River. Founded by Loyalists in 1785 near the former Acadian settlement of Sainte-Anne's Point, it was chosen as capital by Governor Thomas Carleton because it was safer from attack than the…

ferryland.s: Ferryland is a town on the east coast of the Avalon Peninsula in Newfoundland, Canada. In 1621 George Calvert, later Lord Baltimore, founded the Colony of Avalon there, which he visited in person in 1627 and 1628 before turning to Maryland.

flinders-island.s: Flinders Island is the largest island of the Furneaux Group in Bass Strait, north-east of Tasmania. From 1833 the surviving Aboriginal Tasmanians, gathered by George Augustus Robinson, were confined at the settlement of Wybalenna on its west coast, where many died of disease.

fremantle.s: Fremantle is a port city at the mouth of the Swan River in Western Australia, part of the Perth metropolitan area. Founded in 1829 with the Swan River Colony, it was named after Captain Charles Fremantle, who claimed the west coast for Britain.

fort-sill.s: Fort Sill is a United States Army post in south-western Oklahoma, founded in 1869 during campaigns against the southern Plains peoples. It served as the agency base for the Kiowa and Comanche reservation, and in 1875 Quanah Parker and the last free Kwahadi Comanche surrendered…

first-anglo-dutch-war.s: The First Anglo-Dutch War of 1652–1654 was a naval war between the Commonwealth of England and the Dutch Republic over trade and shipping, sharpened by the English Navigation Act of 1651. It was fought almost entirely at sea, in battles such as the Kentish Knock, Portland and…

foligno.s: Foligno is a town in Umbria, central Italy, in the plain below Assisi on the old Via Flaminia. A medieval commune and rival of Perugia, it was ruled by the Trinci family from 1305 until the papacy took it in 1439.

fontana-maggiore.s: The Fontana Maggiore is a medieval fountain in the main square of Perugia, completed in 1278 to mark the arrival of an aqueduct bringing water to the hilltop city. Its two polygonal marble basins are carved with reliefs of the months, the liberal arts, biblical scenes and…

francesco-di-marco-datini.s: Francesco di Marco Datini was a merchant of Prato who made his fortune in Avignon and built a network of companies across Italy, Spain and southern France. He left his wealth to a charitable foundation for the poor of Prato.

francisco-de-lima-e-silva.s: Francisco de Lima e Silva was a Brazilian general and politician. In 1824 he commanded the imperial forces that suppressed the Confederation of the Equator in Pernambuco.

force-publique.s: The Force Publique was the army and police force of the Congo Free State and the Belgian Congo, created in 1885–1886, with African soldiers under European officers. Under Leopold II it enforced rubber quotas through hostage-taking, floggings and mutilations.

fulk-i-count-of-anjou.s: Fulk I, called the Red, was the first count of Anjou of the Ingelger dynasty and the son of Ingelger. Building on his father's position around Angers, he became viscount and was styled count by about 930, turning a frontier command against Bretons and Vikings into a hereditary…

fezensac.s: Fezensac was a medieval county in Gascony, south-western France, centred on Vic-Fezensac and the city of Auch. It was created in the 10th century for a son of the dukes of Gascony, and its counts were closely related to those of Armagnac, who inherited it in the 12th century.

fors-de-bigorre.s: The Fors de Bigorre is a charter of customary law granted around 1097 by the count of Bigorre, in the central Pyrenees, setting out the rights of the inhabitants and limits on the count's power. Among the oldest written customs of the Pyrenees, it regulated justice, military…

forcalquier.s: Forcalquier is a hill town in the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department of south-eastern France. From the 11th century to 1209 it was the capital of a county formed from the inheritance of the counts of Provence, covering the Durance valley and Sisteron.

fils-river.s: The Fils is a river in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, about 63 km long and a right tributary of the Neckar. It rises on the Swabian Jura near Wiesensteig and flows past Geislingen an der Steige and Göppingen to join the Neckar at Plochingen.

floris-v-count-of-holland.s: Floris V (1254–1296) was Count of Holland and Zeeland from 1256. He conquered the West Frisians, granted charters to towns and favoured townsmen and peasants against the nobility, earning the name 'god of the peasants'.

frauenfeld.s: Frauenfeld is a town in north-eastern Switzerland, capital of the canton of Thurgau, on the Murg. It was founded around 1246 near a castle of the counts of Kyburg, passed to the Habsburgs in 1264 and to the Swiss Confederates with the Thurgau in 1460.

feldkirch.s: Feldkirch is a town in the Austrian state of Vorarlberg, on the Ill near the borders with Switzerland and Liechtenstein. It was founded around 1200 by Count Hugo I of Montfort below his Schattenburg castle and was sold to the Habsburgs in 1375.

friedrich-joachim-stengel.s: Friedrich Joachim Stengel (1694–1787) was a German Baroque architect who served the princes of Nassau-Saarbrücken as their master builder. He shaped Saarbrücken as a Baroque residence, designing the Ludwigskirche, the palace and the Ludwigsplatz ensemble, as well as churches,…

francis-i-duke-of-nevers.s: Francis I, Duke of Nevers, born François de Clèves, was a French nobleman and soldier of the house of Cleves, which had held the county of Nevers since 1491. In 1539 Francis I of France raised Nevers to a duchy-peerage for him, making him its first duke.

franco-ottoman-alliance.s: The Franco-Ottoman alliance was the long-lasting partnership between the Kingdom of France and the Ottoman Empire, formed by Francis I and Suleiman the Magnificent against the Habsburgs and formalised in 1536. Its best-known joint action was the siege of Nice in 1543, after…

fraxinetum.s: Fraxinetum was a fortified base set up by Muslim adventurers from al-Andalus around 890 near modern La Garde-Freinet, in the Maures hills of Provence. From it raiders controlled Alpine passes, plundered monasteries and in 972 captured Abbot Majolus of Cluny.

frederick-vii-count-of-toggenburg.s: Frederick VII was the last Count of Toggenburg, ruling a large territory in eastern Switzerland that stretched from the Toggenburg valley to the Prättigau and Davos. He allied with both Zürich and Schwyz, and when he died without heirs in 1436 their rival claims to his lands…

frederick-vii-of-denmark.s: Frederick VII was King of Denmark from 1848 until his death in 1863, the last of the senior Oldenburg line. In 1849 he signed the June Constitution, which ended absolute monarchy and made Denmark a constitutional monarchy.

ferdinand-i-of-aragon.s: Ferdinand I, known as Ferdinand of Antequera, was King of Aragon from 1412 to 1416. A Castilian prince of the Trastámara dynasty and regent of Castile, he won fame by taking Antequera from Granada in 1410.

frederick-iii-of-wied.s: Frederick III of Wied was a German count who founded the town of Neuwied on the Rhine in 1653, near a village ruined in the Thirty Years' War. To attract settlers he promised freedom of religion and trade privileges, and Neuwied became a refuge for religious minorities,…

fulda-abbey.s: Fulda Abbey was a Benedictine monastery in Hesse, Germany, founded in 744 by Sturm, a disciple of Saint Boniface, who was buried there in 754. Under abbots such as Rabanus Maurus it became one of the leading centres of learning in the Carolingian empire.

francisco-de-montejo.s: Francisco de Montejo was a Spanish conquistador who served under Hernán Cortés and in 1526 received a royal contract to conquer Yucatán. His campaigns from 1527 met fierce Maya resistance and were abandoned for a time; the conquest was completed by his son and nephew of the…

fiachnae-mac-demmain.s: Fiachnae mac Demmáin was a king of the Dál Fiatach and of the Ulaid in the early 7th century. He contested the overkingship of the Ulaid with his namesake Fiachnae mac Báetáin of the Dál nAraidi, whom he defeated and killed in 626, and he was himself killed in battle the…

fiachnae-mac-baetain.s: Fiachnae mac Báetáin was a king of the Dál nAraidi and of the Ulaid who died in 626. One of the most powerful rulers in the north of Ireland in his day, he is said to have campaigned in Britain, and he was killed in battle by Fiachnae mac Demmáin of the Dál Fiatach.

flintshire.s: Flintshire is a county in north-east Wales on the southern shore of the Dee estuary, bordering England, with its administrative centre at Mold. It was created in 1284 by the Statute of Rhuddlan after Edward I's conquest of Wales, and Flint Castle was one of his first Welsh…

fort-casimir.s: Fort Casimir was a Dutch fort built in 1651 on the Delaware River by Peter Stuyvesant to challenge the colony of New Sweden. The Swedes seized it in 1654 and renamed it Fort Trinity, prompting the Dutch to conquer all of New Sweden in 1655.

failaka-island.s: Failaka is an island in the Persian Gulf off Kuwait City. In the Bronze Age it was an outpost of the Dilmun culture, with settlements, temples and seals of Dilmun type, and in the Hellenistic period it held a fortress and temples under the Seleucids, when it was known as Ikaros.

front-for-the-restoration-of-unity-and-d.n: Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy
front-for-the-restoration-of-unity-and-d.s: The Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy (FRUD) is a political movement of the Afar people of Djibouti, formed in 1991. It launched an armed rebellion that year against the government of Hassan Gouled Aptidon, protesting at the dominance of the Issa Somali.

francis-nicholson.s: Francis Nicholson was an English army officer and colonial administrator who governed several American colonies. As lieutenant governor of New York under Sir Edmund Andros in the Dominion of New England, he was driven out by Leisler's Rebellion in 1689.

fyodor-sergeyev.s: Fyodor Sergeyev, known as Artyom, was a Russian Bolshevik revolutionary who organised workers in the Donbas and spent several years in exile in Australia. In 1918 he headed the short-lived Donetsk–Krivoy Rog Soviet Republic, arguing that the industrial region belonged with…

freising.s: Freising is a town in Upper Bavaria, Germany, on the Isar north of Munich. Saint Corbinian worked there around 720, and in 739 Saint Boniface made it the seat of a bishopric, whose prince-bishops ruled a small territory until 1802; the see moved to Munich in 1821.

frauenkirche-munich.s: The Frauenkirche is the cathedral of the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising. Built in brick between 1468 and 1488 under Duke Sigismund and then Duke Albert IV, to designs by Jörg von Halsbach, it was consecrated in 1494.

first-war-of-castro.s: The First War of Castro was fought from 1641 to 1644 between Pope Urban VIII, supported by his Barberini nephews, and Odoardo Farnese, Duke of Parma, over the Duchy of Castro and the Farnese family's debts. Venice, Tuscany and Modena joined Parma against papal expansion.

fortezza-da-basso.s: The Fortezza da Basso is a fortress in Florence built from 1534 for Duke Alessandro de' Medici to designs by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger. Placed to overawe the citizens rather than to defend against outside enemies, it symbolised the end of republican Florence.

ferrante-ii-gonzaga.s: Ferrante II Gonzaga was Count and from 1621 Duke of Guastalla, a grandson of Ferrante I Gonzaga. A poet and diplomat in Habsburg service, he obtained from Emperor Ferdinand II the elevation of Guastalla to a duchy.

friedrichstadt.s: Friedrichstadt is a small town in Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, founded in 1621 by Duke Frederick III of Holstein-Gottorp for Dutch Remonstrants fleeing persecution. Built in Dutch style with canals and gabled houses, it was meant to become a trading centre and offered freedom…

francis-i-holy-roman-emperor.s: Francis I (1708–1765), born Francis Stephen, was Duke of Lorraine from 1729 until 1737, when he gave up the duchy under the settlement of the War of the Polish Succession and received the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in exchange. His marriage to Maria Theresa in 1736 founded the…

francis-iv-duke-of-modena.s: Francis IV (1779–1846) was Duke of Modena and Reggio from 1814, the first ruler of the House of Austria-Este, and from 1829 also Duke of Massa and Carrara. A conservative ally of Austria, he repressed liberal and nationalist movements.

friedland-mecklenburg.s: Friedland is a small town in the Mecklenburgische Seenplatte district of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Germany, east of Neubrandenburg. It was founded in 1244 by the margraves of Brandenburg and passed to Mecklenburg around 1300 with the Lordship of Stargard.

filippo-maria-visconti.s: Filippo Maria Visconti (1392–1447) was Duke of Milan from 1412, the last of the Visconti line. He rebuilt the state of his father, Gian Galeazzo, after its collapse and waged long wars against Venice and Florence, relying on condottieri such as Francesco Sforza, to whom he…

francesco-maria-pico.s: Francesco Maria Pico (1688–1747) was the last Duke of Mirandola. During the War of the Spanish Succession he sided with France, and in 1708 Emperor Joseph I deprived him of the duchy.

fecamp-abbey.s: Fécamp Abbey is a Benedictine abbey in the town of Fécamp on the Channel coast of Normandy. Refounded by the dukes of Normandy, it was reformed by William of Volpiano around 1001 and became one of the richest and most influential monasteries of the duchy.

friuli.s: Friuli is a historical region of north-eastern Italy between the Alps, the Adriatic and the Isonzo, now part of Friuli-Venezia Giulia. It takes its name from the Roman town of Forum Iulii, modern Cividale.

friedenstein-palace.s: Friedenstein Palace is the residence built in Gotha, Thuringia, between 1643 and 1654 by Duke Ernest the Pious of Saxe-Gotha. Its name, meaning "rock of peace", reflects hopes for the end of the Thirty Years' War.

fritz-steinbach.s: Fritz Steinbach was a German conductor and composer. As director of the Meiningen court orchestra from 1886 to 1903 he became one of the most admired interpreters of Johannes Brahms, who approved his performances of the symphonies.

friedrich-schiller.s: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet, dramatist, historian and philosopher. His first play, The Robbers (1781), was followed by Don Carlos, the Wallenstein trilogy, Mary Stuart and William Tell.

franz-liszt.s: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer, pianist and teacher, the most celebrated piano virtuoso of the nineteenth century. After years of touring, he settled in Weimar as court Kapellmeister from 1848 to 1861, where he conducted works by Wagner and Berlioz and created the…

first-schleswig-war.s: The First Schleswig War was fought from 1848 to 1851 between Denmark and the Schleswig-Holstein rebels, supported by Prussia and the German Confederation, over the future of the duchies of Schleswig and Holstein. After foreign pressure forced Prussia to withdraw, the Danes…

faroald-i-of-spoleto.s: Faroald I was the first Lombard Duke of Spoleto, ruling from around 570 until about 591. Soon after the Lombard invasion of Italy he seized Spoleto in the Umbrian Apennines and raided Byzantine territory, briefly taking the port of Classe near Ravenna.

francis-duke-of-teck.s: Francis, Duke of Teck, was the son of Duke Alexander of Württemberg and a Hungarian countess; because of this unequal marriage he was excluded from the Württemberg succession. He was created Prince of Teck in 1863 and Duke of Teck in 1871.

frederick-the-fair.s: Frederick the Fair was a Habsburg Duke of Austria and Styria from 1308 and German anti-king from 1314, elected by one faction against Louis IV of Bavaria. Defeated and captured by Louis at the Battle of Mühldorf in 1322, he was held prisoner until 1325, when the two rivals…

francesco-maria-ii-della-rovere.s: Francesco Maria II della Rovere was the last Duke of Urbino, ruling from 1574. A learned and pious prince, he fought at the Battle of Lepanto in 1571 and later lived mostly in retirement.

fort-gustavus.s: Fort Gustavus was the Dutch fort at Chinsurah on the Hooghly River in Bengal, headquarters of the Dutch East India Company's directorate of Bengal. It protected the company's warehouses and residences and was the centre of its trade in Bengal textiles, silk and saltpetre.

frans-post.s: Frans Post was a Dutch painter from Haarlem, the first European artist to paint landscapes of the Americas. He travelled to Dutch Brazil with Johan Maurits of Nassau-Siegen and worked there from 1637 to 1644.

fort-geldria.s: Fort Geldria was the Dutch fort at Pulicat, on the Coromandel Coast of south-eastern India, built in 1613. It was the headquarters of the Dutch East India Company's Coromandel governorate for most of the 17th century and a base for the textile and slave trades with South-East…

frederick-coyett.s: Frederick Coyett was a Swedish-born official of the Dutch East India Company and the last governor of Dutch Formosa, from 1656 to 1662. After a nine-month siege of Fort Zeelandia by Koxinga's forces he surrendered in February 1662.

fort-frederik-hendrik.s: Fort Frederik Hendrik was the first Dutch settlement on Mauritius, founded by the Dutch East India Company in 1638 at Grand Port on the island's south-east coast. Named after the stadtholder Frederick Henry, it supplied passing ships with timber, meat and water.

franconia.s: Franconia is a historical region of southern Germany centred on the valley of the Main, now mostly in northern Bavaria with parts in Baden-Württemberg, Thuringia and Hesse. One of the stem duchies of East Francia, it was dominated in the early 10th century by the Conradines,…

faynan.s: Faynan is a copper-rich district on the eastern side of the Arabah valley in southern Jordan. Mined from the Neolithic onwards, it reached peaks of production in the Early Bronze Age, in the Iron Age, when the smelting site of Khirbat en-Nahas flourished, and in the Roman…

frederick-iii-elector-of-saxony.s: Frederick III, Elector of Saxony, known as Frederick the Wise, ruled the Ernestine electorate from 1486 to 1525. He founded the University of Wittenberg in 1502, where Martin Luther taught, and protected Luther after his condemnation, refusing to surrender him after the Diet…

frederick-peake.s: Frederick Peake, known as Peake Pasha, was a British army officer who founded and commanded the Arab Legion, the army of the Emirate of Transjordan, from the early 1920s until 1939. He built it from local police and gendarmerie units into a force that kept order and secured…

fluvia.s: The Fluvià is a river in the province of Girona in Catalonia, north-eastern Spain, about 97 kilometres long. It rises in the volcanic district of La Garrotxa, flows past the medieval town of Besalú and reaches the Mediterranean in the Gulf of Roses, near the ancient Greek…

fuad-safar.s: Fuad Safar was an Iraqi archaeologist and one of the founders of archaeology in modern Iraq. Working for the Iraqi Directorate of Antiquities, he excavated Tell Hassuna and Eridu with Seton Lloyd in the 1940s, uncovering the long sequence of temples at Eridu, and later…

falerii-novi.s: Falerii Novi was the new town founded on open ground after Rome destroyed the Faliscan hill city of Falerii in 241 BCE and moved its inhabitants there. It lies near Fabrica di Roma in northern Lazio, and its circuit of walls, over 2 km long with dozens of towers and the gate…

falkland-islands-company.s: The Falkland Islands Company is a British trading company incorporated by royal charter in 1851 to develop the Falkland Islands. It became the islands' largest landowner and employer, running sheep farms that exported wool to Britain, as well as shipping and the main stores in…

faereyinga-saga.s: Færeyinga saga is an Icelandic saga written around 1200 that tells the history of the Faroe Islands from their settlement to the early 11th century. Its central story is the long feud between Sigmundur Brestisson, who brought Christianity to the islands on behalf of King Olaf…

front-for-the-liberation-of-occupied-sou.n: Front for the Liberation of Occupied South Yemen
front-for-the-liberation-of-occupied-sou.s: The Front for the Liberation of Occupied South Yemen (FLOSY) was a nationalist movement formed in 1966 and backed by Nasser's Egypt, which fought the British in Aden during the Aden Emergency. It competed violently with the more radical National Liberation Front for control of…

firozpur.s: Firozpur, historically Ferozepur, is a city in the Indian state of Punjab near the Sutlej river and the border with Pakistan. Under Sikh sardars from the 1760s, it came under British protection in 1809 and was annexed in 1835, becoming a major British cantonment and base for…

firth-of-tay.s: The Firth of Tay is the estuary of the River Tay on the east coast of Scotland, separating Fife to the south from Angus and the city of Dundee to the north. In the early Middle Ages it marked a boundary between Pictish territories.

finnish-peoples-delegation.s: The Finnish People's Delegation was the revolutionary government of the Red side in the Finnish Civil War, formed by the Social Democrats when the Red Guards seized Helsinki on 28 January 1918. Chaired by Kullervo Manner, it ruled the industrial south of Finland and proclaimed…

fu-hong.s: Fu Hong was a chieftain of the Di people of eastern Gansu and the founder of the family that ruled the Former Qin state. He served the Later Zhao dynasty as a general and moved his people east under its rule.

fu-sheng.s: Fu Sheng was emperor of the Former Qin state in northern China from 355 to 357. The son of Fu Jian, founder of the state, he is described in the histories as violent and cruel, executing officials and relatives at will.

fet-y-de-las-jons.s: FET y de las JONS was the single party of Francoist Spain, created by Francisco Franco's decree of unification in April 1937, which merged the fascist Falange Española de las JONS with the Carlist traditionalists under his own leadership. It controlled the official trade…

florestan-i-prince-of-monaco.s: Florestan I was Prince of Monaco from 1841 to 1856, a younger son of Honoré IV who had earlier worked as an actor in Paris. His government, largely run by his wife Caroline Gibert, imposed monopolies and taxes that provoked the revolt of 1848, when Menton and Roquebrune broke…

french-national-committee.s: The French National Committee was the governing body of Free France, set up by Charles de Gaulle in London in September 1941. Its members held portfolios like ministers, and it gained growing recognition from the Allies as the representative of fighting France.

federsee.s: The Federsee is a lake in Upper Swabia, Baden-Württemberg, surrounded by the largest moor in south-western Germany. The moor has preserved the remains of many Neolithic and Bronze Age settlements, including the Wasserburg Buchau, and is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site…

ferdinand-von-zeppelin.s: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin was a German army officer from Konstanz who developed the rigid airship. His first airship, LZ 1, flew over Lake Constance from Friedrichshafen in 1900, and his company Luftschiffbau Zeppelin built airships used for passenger travel and as bombers…

fettmilch-uprising.s: The Fettmilch Uprising was a revolt of guildsmen in Frankfurt am Main from 1612 to 1616, led by the gingerbread baker Vincenz Fettmilch against the patrician council. In August 1614 the rioters plundered the Judengasse and expelled the city's Jews.

frankfurt-judengasse.s: The Judengasse was the walled Jewish quarter of Frankfurt am Main, to which the city confined its Jews from 1462. Its single narrow street became one of the most crowded places in Europe, and it was the birthplace of the Rothschild banking family.

friedberg-hesse.s: Friedberg is a town in the Wetterau north of Frankfurt in Hesse, founded by the Hohenstaufen beside an imperial castle on a ridge. The town, an imperial city by 1211, and the castle community of the Burgraviate of Friedberg, governed by knights, were rival neighbours for…

francis-duke-of-guise.s: Francis, Duke of Guise, was a French general and leader of the Catholic party. He defended Metz against Emperor Charles V in the siege of 1552–1553 and took Calais from the English in 1558.

fecht.s: The Fecht is a river in Alsace, France, that rises in the Vosges and flows east through the Munster valley and Turckheim to join the Ill north of Colmar. Its valley was long a route across the Vosges into Lorraine, and the abbey of Munster lay on its upper course.

fossa-carolina.s: The Fossa Carolina was a canal that Charlemagne ordered dug in 793 near Treuchtlingen in Bavaria to link the Rhine and Danube river systems through the Altmühl and the Rezat. The work was abandoned unfinished, apparently because of rain and soft ground, but a stretch of the…

franconian-jura.s: The Franconian Jura is a low limestone upland in northern Bavaria, running in an arc from the Ries crater north to the Main valley. It is known for its caves, dry valleys and quarries of Jurassic limestone, including the fine plate limestone of Solnhofen, and its northern part…

franz-von-papen.s: Franz von Papen was a German Catholic conservative politician who was chancellor of Germany in 1932. He deposed the Social Democratic-led government of Prussia in July 1932 and in January 1933 helped persuade President Hindenburg to appoint Adolf Hitler as chancellor, serving…

francois-mitterrand.s: François Mitterrand was a French Socialist politician and president of France from 1981 to 1995, the longest-serving president of the Fifth Republic. His election brought the left to power for the first time under that constitution; he abolished the death penalty,…

french-directory.s: The French Directory was the five-member executive that governed the French First Republic from November 1795 to November 1799 under the Constitution of the Year III. It faced financial crisis, corruption and repeated coups against royalists and Jacobins, while its armies,…

francois-xavier-donzelot.s: François-Xavier Donzelot was a French general of the Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars. He served in Bonaparte's Egyptian campaign and from 1807 governed the Ionian Islands, holding Corfu under British blockade after Britain took most of the other islands in 1809–1810.

fyodor-ushakov.s: Fyodor Ushakov was a Russian admiral who never lost a battle, commanding the Black Sea Fleet in victories over the Ottomans at Kerch Strait, Tendra and Kaliakra in 1790–1791. In 1798–1799, allied with the Ottomans, he led a joint fleet that took the Ionian Islands from France,…

felix-houphouet-boigny.s: Félix Houphouët-Boigny was the first president of Ivory Coast, from independence in 1960 until his death in 1993. A physician and wealthy planter, he founded the African Agricultural Union in 1944, sat in the French National Assembly, where he secured the abolition of forced…

fort-maurepas.s: Fort Maurepas was a French fort built in 1699 by Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville on the eastern shore of Biloxi Bay, at present-day Ocean Springs, Mississippi. It was the first seat of the French colony of Louisiana and the base for exploring the lower Mississippi.

fangataufa.s: Fangataufa is an uninhabited atoll in the Tuamotu archipelago of French Polynesia, south of Moruroa. With Moruroa, it was the site of France's Pacific nuclear tests from 1966 to 1996; it hosted the first French thermonuclear test, Canopus, in August 1968, and later underground…

falloux-laws.s: The Falloux Laws were French education laws passed in 1850 and 1851 under the Second Republic, named after the education minister Frédéric de Falloux. They allowed the Catholic Church and other bodies to open secondary schools freely and increased clerical influence over state…

four-communes.s: The Four Communes were the colonial towns of Saint-Louis, Gorée, Rufisque and Dakar in Senegal, whose inhabitants, the originaires, enjoyed French civil and political rights, unlike the subjects of the rest of French West Africa. Given municipal status between 1872 and 1887,…

fortore.s: The Fortore is a river of southern Italy, about 110 km long, rising in the Apennines of Campania and flowing north-east through Molise and Apulia to the Adriatic. Its valley formed the south-eastern limit of the land of the Frentani in antiquity.

frisia.s: Frisia is the coastal region along the southern North Sea inhabited by the Frisians, which in its widest early medieval extent reached from the Zwin near Bruges to the Weser. Conquered by the Franks in the 8th century, its lands were later divided between the Dutch province of…

fukui.s: Fukui is the capital of Fukui Prefecture on the Sea of Japan side of central Honshu. It grew around Kitanoshō Castle, built by Shibata Katsuie in the 1570s, and from 1601 was the castle town of the Fukui domain of the Echizen Matsudaira family.

fukui-prefecture.s: Fukui Prefecture is a prefecture of Japan on the Sea of Japan coast of central Honshu, with its capital at Fukui. Formed after the abolition of the domains in 1871 and given its present shape in 1881, it covers the old provinces of Echizen and Wakasa.

freiburg-im-breisgau.s: Freiburg im Breisgau is a city in Baden-Württemberg, south-western Germany, on the edge of the Black Forest. Founded by the Zähringen dukes in 1120, it passed to the Habsburgs in 1368 and was the chief town of Further Austria, later its seat of government, until it went to…

francis-younghusband.s: Francis Younghusband was a British army officer and explorer of Central Asia. In 1903 and 1904 he led the British expedition to Tibet, which killed hundreds of poorly armed Tibetans at Chumik Shenko, reached Lhasa and imposed a treaty opening Tibet to British trade.

federal-convention-german-confederation.s: The Federal Convention, usually called the Federal Diet, was the only central institution of the German Confederation from 1815 to 1866. It sat in Frankfurt, in the Thurn und Taxis palace, as a permanent congress of envoys from the member states, with Austria presiding.

finschhafen.s: Finschhafen is a town on the Huon Peninsula in Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea. Founded in 1885 by the German New Guinea Company and named after the explorer Otto Finsch, it was the first capital of German New Guinea until disease forced the administration to move in 1891.

firozkoh.s: Firozkoh was the summer capital of the Ghurid dynasty in the mountains of Ghor, in central Afghanistan. Its exact site was lost after the Mongols destroyed it in the 1220s, but it is usually placed in the valley of the Minaret of Jam, built by the Ghurid sultan Ghiyath al-Din…

first-battle-of-tarain.s: The First Battle of Tarain was fought in 1191 near Taraori in present-day Haryana, India, between the Ghurid army of Muhammad of Ghor and the Rajput forces of Prithviraj Chauhan, king of Ajmer and Delhi. The Rajputs won, and Muhammad of Ghor was wounded and carried from the…

friedrich-hecker.s: Friedrich Hecker was a lawyer and radical democrat from Baden who led an armed rising for a German republic in April 1848, the Hecker Uprising, which was defeated near Kandern. He fled to Switzerland and then to the United States, where he farmed in Illinois and served as a…

ferdinando-i-de-medici.s: Ferdinando I de' Medici was Grand Duke of Tuscany from 1587 to 1609. A cardinal who gave up his office to succeed his brother Francesco I, he governed ably, developed Livorno as a free port open to Jews and other foreign merchants through the Livornine laws of 1591–1593,…

farshut.s: Farshut is a town in Qena Governorate in Upper Egypt, near the Nile bend at Nag Hammadi. In the 17th and 18th centuries it was the seat of the Hawwara Arab sheikhs, who ruled much of Upper Egypt as tax farmers under Ottoman Egypt and reached their height under Shaykh Hammam…

faiyum.s: The Faiyum is a large depression and oasis west of the Nile, south-west of Cairo, watered by a branch of the river, the Bahr Yusuf, and containing Lake Qarun. Twelfth Dynasty kings, especially Amenemhat III, reclaimed land there, and the Ptolemies settled Greek veterans in it.

ferentino.s: Ferentino, ancient Ferentinum, is a hill town of the Hernici in the Sacco valley of southern Lazio, Italy. It is known for its massive polygonal walls and its acropolis of the pre-Roman and Roman periods.

feis-temro.s: The Feis Temro, or Feast of Tara, was a ceremony held at Tara in early medieval Ireland, in which a new king of Tara was inaugurated through a symbolic marriage to the goddess of sovereignty. Irish annals record its last celebration under Diarmait mac Cerbaill around 560, and…

ferdinand-von-hompesch-zu-bolheim.s: Ferdinand von Hompesch zu Bolheim was the last Grand Master of the Knights Hospitaller to rule Malta, and the first German to hold the office, elected in 1797. In June 1798 Napoleon's fleet, on its way to Egypt, demanded entry, and Hompesch surrendered the island without…

foulques-de-villaret.s: Foulques de Villaret was Grand Master of the Knights Hospitaller from 1305 to 1319. Seeking a base of the order's own after the loss of the Holy Land, he began the conquest of Byzantine Rhodes in 1306, and the city fell around 1309-1310.

fidesz.s: Fidesz is a Hungarian political party founded in 1988 as a liberal alliance of young democrats, which under Viktor Orbán moved to national conservatism. It governed from 1998 to 2002 and won a two-thirds majority in 2010, which it used to adopt a new constitution, the…

fatima-al-fihri.s: Fatima al-Fihri was a woman from Kairouan who settled in Fez in the Idrisid period with her family. Using her inheritance, she founded the al-Qarawiyyin mosque in 859, which grew into one of the leading centres of Islamic learning.

fergana-valley.s: The Fergana Valley is a fertile basin in Central Asia, drained by the Syr Darya and shared today by Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. Chinese sources of the Han period knew it as Dayuan, famed for its horses.

fugumba.s: Fugumba is a town in the Futa Jallon highlands of central Guinea. It was the religious centre of the Imamate of Futa Jallon, where the council of elders met and where each new almamy was invested before taking office at the capital Timbo.

futa-toro.s: Futa Toro is a region along the middle Senegal river, on the border of present-day Senegal and Mauritania, home of the Fulbe and Toucouleur peoples. It was the seat of the Denianke kingdom from the 16th century, until Muslim clerics overthrew it and founded an Islamic imamate…

frowin-of-engelberg.s: Frowin was abbot of Engelberg in central Switzerland from 1143 until his death in 1178. Coming from St. Blaise Abbey in the Black Forest, he built up the young monastery's library and scriptorium, which produced fine illuminated manuscripts, and wrote theological works,…

franz-georg-von-metternich.s: Franz Georg von Metternich was a Rhenish count and diplomat in Habsburg service, the father of the Austrian chancellor Klemens von Metternich. He served as Austrian minister in the Austrian Netherlands until the French conquest.

franz-joseph-spiegler.s: Franz Joseph Spiegler was a German painter of the late baroque, active mainly in upper Swabia and around Lake Constance. His largest work is the cycle of ceiling frescoes in the abbey church of Zwiefalten, painted from 1751, whose nave fresco is one of the largest of the period.

francis-burton-harrison.s: Francis Burton Harrison was an American Democratic politician who served as Governor-General of the Philippines from 1913 to 1921 under President Woodrow Wilson. He rapidly replaced American officials with Filipinos and worked closely with Filipino leaders such as Manuel…

fianna-fail.s: Fianna Fáil is an Irish political party founded in 1926 by Éamon de Valera and opponents of the Anglo-Irish Treaty. It entered government in 1932 and became the dominant party of independent Ireland, leading most governments for the rest of the century.

fuman.s: Fuman is a town in Gilan province in northern Iran, west of Rasht, at the foot of the Alborz range. In the late Middle Ages it was the seat of the Ishaqid rulers of western Gilan before Rasht overtook it.

francesco-melzi-deril.s: Francesco Melzi d'Eril was a Milanese aristocrat and statesman who served as vice-president of the Italian Republic from 1802 to 1805, under Napoleon as president. He built an effective administration, reformed finances and negotiated a concordat with the papacy.

flores-guatemala.s: Flores is a town on an island in Lake Petén Itzá in northern Guatemala and the capital of Petén department. It stands on the site of Nojpetén, the capital of the Itza Maya kingdom, which the Spanish conquered in 1697.

firhun-ag-alinsar.s: Firhun ag Alinsar was amenokal, paramount chief, of the Iwellemmeden Kel Ataram Tuareg in what is now Mali. Made to submit to the French, he was imprisoned, escaped and in 1916, during the First World War, led a revolt against French rule in the Niger region.

froso-runestone.s: The Frösö Runestone is an 11th-century runestone on the island of Frösön in Jämtland, Sweden, and the northernmost Viking Age runestone in the country. Its inscription states that Östman, son of Gudfast, raised the stone, built a bridge and had Jämtland Christianised, making…

froson.s: Frösön is an island in the lake Storsjön in Jämtland, central Sweden, opposite the town of Östersund. Its name derives from the god Frey, and it was a pre-Christian cult centre and the meeting place of the Jamtamót, the assembly of the self-governing Jämtland farmers.

faramurz.s: Faramurz was the son and successor of Ala al-Dawla Muhammad, founder of the Kakuyid dynasty, and ruled Isfahan from 1041. Pressed by the rising Seljuk Empire, he surrendered Isfahan to Sultan Tughril in 1051 and received Yazd and Abarkuh instead.

finns.s: The Finns are a Finnic people of northern Europe, the majority population of Finland, speaking a Uralic language. In the Middle Ages the groups that formed them, including the Finns proper of the south-west, the Tavastians and the Karelians, were drawn into the rivalry between…

filipp-goloshchekin.s: Filipp Goloshchekin was a Bolshevik official who, as a leader in the Urals, helped organise the execution of the Romanov family in 1918. As first secretary of the Communist Party in Kazakhstan from 1925 to 1933 he pushed forced collectivisation and the settlement of the…

francisco-combes.s: Francisco Combes was a Spanish Jesuit missionary in the southern Philippines. He worked for years in Mindanao and wrote the Historia de las islas de Mindanao, Iolo y sus adyacentes, published in Madrid in 1667.

flatters-expedition.s: The Flatters expedition was a French mission led by Lieutenant-Colonel Paul Flatters to survey a route for a railway across the Sahara. On its second journey in February 1881 it was attacked by Kel Ahaggar Tuareg in the Ahaggar region; Flatters and most of the party were killed.

fachi.s: Fachi is an oasis in the Ténéré desert of eastern Niger, west of Bilma. Like Bilma it produces salt and dates, which Tuareg caravans from the Aïr carried south to the Hausa lands.

falak-ol-aflak.s: Falak-ol-Aflak is a castle on a hill in the centre of Khorramabad in Lorestan province, western Iran. Its origins are usually traced to the Sasanian period.

fruela-ii-of-asturias.s: Fruela II was king of Asturias from 910 and of León from 924 until his death in 925. A son of Alfonso III the Great, he received Asturias when his father's realm was divided among his sons, and on the death of his brother Ordoño II he took the throne of León, reuniting the…

foumban.s: Foumban is a city in the West Region of Cameroon and the historic capital of the Bamum kingdom. It is the seat of the Bamum sultan, whose palace, built in the 1910s under King Ibrahim Njoya, houses a museum of royal art, and the city is known for its craftsmen in brass and wood.

fort-manuel.s: Fort Manuel was the first European fort in India, built by the Portuguese at Kochi on the Malabar Coast in 1503 with the permission of the ruler of Cochin. Named after King Manuel I of Portugal, it protected the Portuguese trading post and Cochin itself against the Zamorin of…

frankopan-family.s: The Frankopans were a Croatian noble family, originally counts of the island of Krk, who from the 12th century held large estates in western Croatia and along the coast. Among the most powerful magnates of medieval Croatia, they produced bans, built castles and churches and…

finghin-mac-carthaigh.s: Fínghin Mac Carthaigh was king of Desmond in south-west Munster, a member of the MacCarthy dynasty. In 1261 he defeated the Anglo-Norman FitzGeralds at the Battle of Callann, halting their advance into Kerry and Cork, but he was killed later that year attacking the castle of…

felix-of-burgundy.s: Felix of Burgundy was the missionary bishop who brought Christianity to East Anglia. Coming from Burgundy, he was sent by Archbishop Honorius of Canterbury and welcomed by King Sigeberht around 630, establishing his see at Dommoc and a school.

felix-of-aquitaine.s: Felix of Aquitaine was a Gallo-Roman nobleman of Toulouse who ruled Aquitaine as duke or patrician around the 660s, largely independent of the Merovingian kings. His rule is poorly documented, but he stands at the start of the line of Aquitanian rulers that continued with…

felix-zu-schwarzenberg.s: Felix zu Schwarzenberg was an Austrian prince and statesman who became minister-president of the Austrian Empire in November 1848, during the revolutions of that year. He installed the young Franz Joseph as emperor, crushed the Hungarian revolution with Russian help, restored…

farouk-of-egypt.s: Farouk was king of Egypt from 1936 to 1952, a member of the Muhammad Ali dynasty. His reign was marked by British interference, including the Abdeen Palace incident of 1942, defeat in the 1948 Arab–Israeli War and growing public anger at corruption.

faleme-river.s: The Falémé is a river of West Africa, a left-bank tributary of the Senegal, that rises in the Fouta Djallon of Guinea and forms much of the border between Senegal and Mali. Its valley runs through Bambuk, one of the great gold-producing regions of medieval and early modern…

france-preseren.s: France Prešeren was a Romantic poet and the national poet of Slovenia. A lawyer who worked in Ljubljana and Kranj, he wrote in Slovene when German dominated educated life, and his collected Poems and the epic 'The Baptism on the Savica' raised Slovene literature to a European…

farhud.s: The Farhud was a violent pogrom against the Jews of Baghdad on 1–2 June 1941, in the power vacuum after the fall of Rashid Ali's pro-Axis government and before British troops entered the city. At least 180 Jews were killed, many more were injured and their property was looted.

francesco-crispi.s: Francesco Crispi was an Italian statesman, a Sicilian veteran of Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand, who was prime minister in 1887–1891 and 1893–1896. He pursued a strong executive, close ties with Germany and colonial expansion in East Africa, and harshly suppressed the…

francisco-de-lacerda-e-almeida.s: Francisco José de Lacerda e Almeida was a Brazilian-born Portuguese mathematician and explorer. After surveying the borders of Brazil, he was appointed governor of the Rivers of Sena in Mozambique and in 1798 led an expedition from Tete towards the Kingdom of Kazembe, hoping…

felou-falls.s: The Felou Falls are rapids and falls on the Senegal River near Médine, a few kilometres upstream from Kayes in western Mali. They mark the upper limit of navigation from the Atlantic, which made the nearby post of Médine an important river port and trading station in the 19th…

fianarantsoa.s: Fianarantsoa is a city in the southern highlands of Madagascar and the main town of the Betsileo region. It was founded in 1830 by the Merina queen Ranavalona I as an administrative centre to control the conquered Betsileo, and it became a centre of education, Christianity and…

ferns.s: Ferns is a village in County Wexford, Ireland, once the royal seat of the kings of Leinster of the Uí Cheinnselaig dynasty. A monastery was founded there by St Máedóc around 600, and it became the seat of a diocese.

feidlimid-mac-crimthainn.s: Feidlimid mac Crimthainn was king of Munster from 820 to 847 and also a churchman, counted as an abbot and bishop. He raided great monasteries such as Clonmacnoise and Kildare and challenged the Uí Néill, pressing a claim to be high king of Ireland.

fourth-anglo-mysore-war.s: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was fought in 1798–1799 between Tipu Sultan of Mysore and the East India Company, allied with the Nizam of Hyderabad. Fearing a French alliance, Governor-General Richard Wellesley sent armies that stormed Srirangapatna on 4 May 1799, where Tipu was…

fon-title.s: Fon is the title of the sacred kings of the chiefdoms and kingdoms of the Cameroon Grassfields, such as Nso, Bafut and Bali-Nyonga. A Fon rules with palace societies and regulatory societies, such as the Kwifon or Ngwerong, which enforce his decisions, carry out royal rituals…

fon-people.s: The Fon are a Gbe-speaking people of southern Benin, living mainly on the Abomey plateau and around Cotonou. They formed the core population of the Kingdom of Dahomey, which rose from the early 17th century and became a major power in the Atlantic slave trade.

fort-canning-hill.s: Fort Canning Hill is a hill in central Singapore overlooking the Singapore River. Malay tradition remembers it as Bukit Larangan, the Forbidden Hill of the kings of Singapura, and excavations there have found 14th-century Chinese ceramics, gold ornaments and workshop remains.

felipe-gonzalez.s: Felipe González is a Spanish politician who led the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party and was prime minister of Spain from 1982 to 1996, the longest term of the democratic period. His governments took Spain into the European Economic Community in 1986, won a referendum to stay…

frithuwold.s: Frithuwold was a sub-king of Surrey in the 670s, ruling under Wulfhere of Mercia, and the only known ruler of the province. He is known from a charter of around 672–674 granting extensive lands along the Thames to Chertsey Abbey.

fishbourne-roman-palace.s: Fishbourne Roman Palace, near Chichester in West Sussex, is the largest known Roman residence in Britain, built around 75 with formal gardens and fine mosaics. Discovered in 1960, it has often been linked to the client king Togidubnus.

feletheus.s: Feletheus, also called Feva, was king of the Rugians north of the Danube in the late 5th century, son of King Flaccitheus. Eugippius' Life of Saint Severinus portrays him and his queen Giso dealing with the saint.

flaccitheus.s: Flaccitheus was king of the Rugians on the middle Danube in the decades after the fall of the Hunnic empire. Eugippius' Life of Saint Severinus describes him seeking the saint's advice when threatened by the Ostrogoths.

fort-portal.s: Fort Portal is a city in western Uganda at the foot of the Rwenzori Mountains. It grew around a British fort of 1893 named after the diplomat Sir Gerald Portal, and became the capital of the Toro kingdom, with the royal palace on a hill above the town.

fitzgeralds-of-kildare.s: The FitzGeralds of Kildare were an Anglo-Norman family who held the earldom of Kildare from 1316, with their seat at Maynooth. In the late 15th and early 16th centuries Garret Mór and Garret Óg FitzGerald, as lords deputy, were the most powerful men in Ireland.

fukuoka-prefecture.s: Fukuoka Prefecture is a prefecture of Japan in northern Kyushu, with its capital at Fukuoka. It was created in 1871 from the Fukuoka domain when the domains were abolished, and took its present form in 1876 by merging with the prefectures formed from Kokura, Kurume and Yanagawa.

federated-states-of-micronesia.s: The Federated States of Micronesia is an island country in the western Pacific made up of four states, Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei and Kosrae, spread across the Caroline Islands. Formerly part of the United Nations Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands administered by the United…

freetown.s: Freetown is the capital and largest city of Sierra Leone, on the Sierra Leone Peninsula at the mouth of the Sierra Leone River. It was founded in 1792 by the Sierra Leone Company as a settlement for freed slaves, including Black Loyalists from Nova Scotia, after the earlier…

fu-jiezi.s: Fu Jiezi was a Han dynasty envoy to the Western Regions in the reign of Emperor Zhao. In 77 BCE he assassinated the king of Loulan, who had sided with the Xiongnu, after which the Han installed a new king and renamed the kingdom Shanshan.

feng-dao.s: Feng Dao was a Chinese official who served as chief minister under several dynasties of the Five Dynasties period, including the Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han and Later Zhou. In 932 he proposed the printing of the Confucian classics from woodblocks, completed in 953, the…
