fotudeng.s: Fotudeng was a Buddhist monk from Central Asia, probably Kucha, who arrived in Luoyang in 310. He became adviser to the Later Zhao rulers Shi Le and Shi Hu, gaining their favour through reputed miracles and prophecies.

firestone-tire-and-rubber-company.s: The Firestone Tire and Rubber Company is an American tyre maker founded by Harvey Firestone in Akron, Ohio, in 1900. In 1926 it obtained a 99-year lease on up to a million acres in Liberia for rubber plantations, tied to a loan to the government, and its Harbel plantation…

francesco-i-gattilusio.s: Francesco I Gattilusio was a Genoese adventurer who helped the Byzantine emperor John V Palaiologos regain his throne from John VI Kantakouzenos in 1354. In reward he received the island of Lesbos and the hand of John V's sister Maria, founding the Gattilusio lordship of Lesbos.

francesca-da-rimini.s: Francesca da Rimini, born Francesca da Polenta, was the daughter of Guido da Polenta, lord of Ravenna, and was married for political reasons to Giovanni Malatesta, called Gianciotto, of Rimini. Around 1285 her husband killed her and his brother Paolo, with whom she had a love…

fano.s: Fano is a coastal town in the Marche, central Italy, on the Adriatic at the end of the Via Flaminia. Founded as the Roman colony of Fanum Fortunae, it keeps an Arch of Augustus.

finlaggan.s: Finlaggan is a site on the island of Islay in the Inner Hebrides, on two small islands in Loch Finlaggan. It was the centre of the Lordship of the Isles, where the lords of Clan Donald were inaugurated and their Council of the Isles met in the 14th and 15th centuries.

fort-st-george.s: Fort St George is the fortress begun by the English East India Company in 1640 at Madraspatnam on the Coromandel Coast, the first English fortress in India. The city of Madras, now Chennai, grew around it, and it was the seat of the Madras Presidency.

firozpur-district.s: Firozpur (Ferozepur) district is a district of Punjab, India, on the Sutlej river along the border with Pakistan. The British took over the town of Firozpur in 1835 and made it a frontier base, and battles of the First Anglo-Sikh War were fought nearby at Mudki and Ferozeshah…

fifteenth-amendment.n: Fifteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution
fifteenth-amendment.s: The Fifteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, ratified in 1870, forbids the federal and state governments to deny a citizen the right to vote because of 'race, color, or previous condition of servitude'. The last of the three Reconstruction amendments, it…

fall-of-the-berlin-wall.s: The fall of the Berlin Wall on the night of 9 November 1989 was the moment when East Germany, facing mass protests and the flight of its citizens to the West, opened the crossings through the wall that had divided Berlin since 1961. A confused announcement that travel…

frederick-douglass.s: Frederick Douglass was an American abolitionist, writer and statesman who escaped slavery in Maryland in 1838 and became the most influential African American of the nineteenth century. His Narrative of 1845 made him famous on both sides of the Atlantic, and his newspaper and…

first-intifada.s: The First Intifada was the Palestinian uprising against Israeli rule in the West Bank and Gaza that began in December 1987 with strikes, boycotts, stone-throwing and mass protest, much of it organised locally rather than by the PLO abroad. Israel could not suppress it quickly,…

fruttuaria-abbey.s: Fruttuaria Abbey was a Benedictine monastery at San Benigno Canavese in Piedmont, founded in 1003 by the reformer William of Volpiano with the support of Arduin of Ivrea, who retired there before his death in 1015. Its Cluniac-style reform spread to many monasteries in…

fritigil.s: Fritigil was a queen of the Marcomanni in the late 4th century. According to Paulinus's Life of Ambrose, she learned of Christianity from a traveller, wrote to Bishop Ambrose of Milan, who sent her a letter of instruction in the faith, and then persuaded her husband to place…

ferdinand-ii-archduke-of-austria.s: Ferdinand II, Archduke of Austria, was a son of Emperor Ferdinand I who ruled Tyrol and Further Austria from 1564. In 1557 he secretly married the commoner Philippine Welser, so their sons were excluded from the succession; one of them, Charles, became Margrave of Burgau.

frederick-i-elector-of-saxony.s: Frederick I, called the Warlike, was a Wettin margrave of Meissen who became the first Wettin Elector of Saxony. He founded the University of Leipzig in 1409, and in 1423 Emperor Sigismund granted him the Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg with its electoral title as a reward for his…

freiberg.s: Freiberg is a town in Saxony, Germany, at the foot of the Ore Mountains. Silver was discovered there around 1168, setting off a mining rush that made the margraves of Meissen rich and the town one of the largest in the region.

fes-el-jdid.s: Fes el-Jdid, 'New Fez', is the royal city founded in 1276 by the Marinid sultan Abu Yusuf Yaqub beside the old city of Fez, Morocco. It held the royal palace (Dar al-Makhzen), barracks and government offices, and in the 15th century the Mellah, the Jewish quarter, grew next to…

finalborgo.s: Finalborgo is a walled medieval town in Liguria, north-western Italy, now part of the municipality of Finale Ligure. It was the seat of the Del Carretto marquises of Finale, whose castle of Gavone stands on the hill above it.

fakhr-al-dawla-ibn-jahir.s: Fakhr al-Dawla Muhammad ibn Jahir was an administrator who served as vizier of the Marwanids of Diyar Bakr and then of the Abbasid caliphs in Baghdad. Around 1085 the Seljuk sultan Malik-Shah I sent him to conquer the Marwanid lands, and after the fall of Amid and Mayyafariqin…

firmus-berber-prince.s: Firmus was a Berber prince of Mauretania, son of the powerful chief Nubel, who led a revolt against Roman rule around 372–375 CE. After a dispute over his father's succession and a quarrel with the Roman count Romanus, he won support from local tribes and some Donatist…

fakhr-al-din-bahramshah.s: Fakhr al-Din Bahramshah was the Mengujekid ruler of Erzincan and Kemah in eastern Anatolia for about sixty years, from the 1160s until his death around 1225. A patron of learning, he received the dedication of Nizami's poem Makhzan al-Asrar.

fu-youde.s: Fu Youde was a general of the founding Hongwu Emperor of the Ming dynasty. In 1371 he led one of the armies that conquered the Ming Xia state in Sichuan, and in the following years he campaigned against the Mongols in the north.

fujian.s: Fujian is a mountainous province on the south-east coast of China, facing Taiwan across the Taiwan Strait, with its capital at Fuzhou. Once the land of the Min Yue people, it was brought under Chinese rule by the Han and settled by Chinese from the north over the following…

fuzhou.s: Fuzhou is the capital of Fujian province in south-eastern China, on the Min river near the coast. As Dongye it was the capital of the Minyue kingdom in the 2nd century BCE, and in the 10th century it was the seat of the Min kingdom.

first-battle-of-bud-dajo.s: The First Battle of Bud Dajo, also called the Moro Crater massacre, was an American assault in March 1906 on Tausug Muslims who had taken refuge in the crater of the volcano Bud Dajo on Jolo in the southern Philippines. Of some 800 to 1,000 people in the crater, including many…

frank-carpenter.s: Frank W. Carpenter was an American colonial official in the Philippines who served as the first civilian governor of the Department of Mindanao and Sulu from 1914 to 1920, after the military-run Moro Province was abolished. He pursued a policy of integrating the Muslim south…

faku.s: Faku was king of the Mpondo in present-day Eastern Cape, South Africa, from the 1820s until his death in 1867. He survived attacks by Shaka's Zulu army, absorbed refugees from the wars of the period and made the Mpondo one of the strongest powers between the Cape and Natal.

flint-river-georgia.s: The Flint River is a river of western Georgia in the United States, flowing south to join the Chattahoochee at the Florida border and form the Apalachicola. Lower Muscogee towns lay along it in the 18th century, and the lands between it and the Ocmulgee were ceded under…

fukuoka.s: Fukuoka is the largest city of Kyushu in south-western Japan and the capital of Fukuoka Prefecture, on Hakata Bay facing Korea. The area was an early gateway for contacts with the continent, from the Yayoi-period state of Na to the medieval port of Hakata.

franciscans.s: The Franciscans are the Catholic religious orders that follow the rule of Francis of Assisi, approved by the papacy between 1209 and 1223, chief among them the Order of Friars Minor. Vowed to poverty and preaching, the friars spread across Europe and became leading…

fort-rosalie.s: Fort Rosalie was a French fort built in 1716 on the bluffs of the lower Mississippi River at present-day Natchez, Mississippi, in the colony of Louisiana. A French settlement and tobacco plantations grew around it on Natchez land.

fuhrer.s: Führer, German for 'leader', was the title used by Adolf Hitler as head of the Nazi Party and, from August 1934, as head of the German state after he merged the offices of president and chancellor on the death of Paul von Hindenburg. The title expressed the Nazi principle that…

frederick-william-koko.s: Frederick William Koko was king of Nembe, also called Brass, in the Niger delta of present-day Nigeria, from 1889. A Christian who later returned to the traditional religion, he led the raid on the Royal Niger Company's depot at Akassa in 1895 in protest at the company's trade…

fredegund.s: Fredegund was queen of the Franks as the wife of Chilperic I, king of Neustria, rising from servant to queen after the murder of his previous wife Galswintha. Her feud with Galswintha's sister Brunhild, queen of Austrasia, fuelled decades of civil war among the Merovingian…

francois-de-laval.s: François de Laval was the first Catholic bishop of Quebec, arriving in New France in 1659 as vicar apostolic and becoming bishop when the diocese was created in 1674. He founded the Seminary of Quebec in 1663, organised parishes and clashed with governors over the sale of…

flushing-queens.s: Flushing is a neighbourhood in the New York City borough of Queens, founded under Dutch rule in 1645 as the English settlement of Vlissingen. In 1657 its residents signed the Flushing Remonstrance, protesting against Director-General Peter Stuyvesant's persecution of Quakers,…

fernando-collor-de-mello.s: Fernando Collor de Mello is a Brazilian politician who in 1989 became the first president elected by direct popular vote since 1960. Taking office in 1990, he froze savings accounts in a failed attempt to halt hyperinflation and opened the economy to foreign trade.

fernando-henrique-cardoso.s: Fernando Henrique Cardoso is a Brazilian sociologist and politician who was president of Brazil from 1995 to 2002. As finance minister in 1993–1994 he introduced the Real Plan, which ended decades of hyperinflation, and its success carried him to the presidency.

faras.s: Faras, ancient Pachoras, was a town on the Nile in Lower Nubia, near the modern border between Egypt and Sudan, now submerged by Lake Nasser. It was the capital of the kingdom of Nobadia and later the seat of a bishop under Makuria.

fujiwara-no-kiyohira.s: Fujiwara no Kiyohira was the founder of the Northern Fujiwara of northern Japan. The son of a Fujiwara father killed in the Former Nine Years' War, he was raised in the Kiyohara family, and after the Later Three Years' War of 1083 to 1087 he became master of Mutsu and Dewa.

fujiwara-no-motohira.s: Fujiwara no Motohira was the second lord of the Northern Fujiwara, who ruled Mutsu and Dewa in northern Japan from Hiraizumi. The son of Kiyohira, he succeeded after a struggle with his brother in 1128 and maintained the family's largely independent power while acknowledging…

fujiwara-no-hidehira.s: Fujiwara no Hidehira was the third lord of the Northern Fujiwara, ruling Mutsu and Dewa from Hiraizumi at the height of the family's wealth. The court made him commander of the northern frontier (chinjufu-shōgun) in 1170.

fujiwara-no-yasuhira.s: Fujiwara no Yasuhira was the fourth and last lord of the Northern Fujiwara of Hiraizumi. Under pressure from Minamoto no Yoritomo, he broke his father Hidehira's promise to protect Minamoto no Yoshitsune and attacked him at Koromogawa in 1189, where Yoshitsune died.

francisco-de-orellana.s: Francisco de Orellana was a Spanish conquistador who made the first known European descent of the Amazon River. Separated from Gonzalo Pizarro's expedition east of Quito, he sailed down the Napo and the Amazon to the Atlantic in 1541–1542, a journey chronicled by the friar…

finistere.s: Finistère is the westernmost department of mainland France, at the tip of the Breton peninsula, with its prefecture at Quimper and the naval port of Brest. Its name comes from the Latin finis terrae, 'end of the land'.

frejus.s: Fréjus is a town in the Var department of south-eastern France, near the Mediterranean coast. It began as Forum Julii, a market town founded by Julius Caesar or his heir, and under Augustus it became a Roman colony and naval base where ships captured at Actium were stationed.

free-aceh-movement.s: The Free Aceh Movement, Gerakan Aceh Merdeka, was a separatist organisation founded in 1976 by Hasan di Tiro to win independence for Aceh from Indonesia. Its insurgency, met by heavy Indonesian military operations, cost thousands of lives.

fossatum-africae.s: The Fossatum Africae was a system of ditches, earth banks and walls built by the Romans along the southern edge of their North African provinces, in modern Algeria and Tunisia, mainly in the 2nd and 3rd centuries CE. Running for hundreds of kilometres in separate sections, it…

fossa-regia.s: The Fossa Regia was a boundary ditch dug by the Romans after the destruction of Carthage in 146 BCE to mark the frontier between their new province of Africa and the kingdom of Numidia. It ran from near Thabraca on the north coast to Thaenae on the east coast of modern Tunisia.

fraomarius.s: Fraomarius was an Alemannic king of the fourth century. Around 371 the emperor Valentinian I, unable to capture Macrianus, made Fraomarius king of the Bucinobantes in his place, but a raid soon devastated the district, and Fraomarius was transferred to Britain as a tribune…

fernando-de-la-rua.s: Fernando de la Rúa was an Argentine Radical Civic Union politician, the first elected head of government of the city of Buenos Aires, and president from 1999 to 2001. Unable to escape recession and debt while keeping the peso pegged to the dollar, his government restricted…

franz-grillparzer.s: Franz Grillparzer was Austria's leading dramatist of the nineteenth century, whose plays, including The Ancestress, King Ottokar's Fortune and Rise and The Waves of Sea and Love, were written largely for the Burgtheater in Vienna. Long hindered by censorship, he was honoured…

franz-schubert.s: Franz Schubert was an Austrian composer, born and active in Vienna, who in a short life wrote more than 600 songs, including the cycles Die schöne Müllerin and Winterreise, as well as symphonies, chamber music and piano works. Little known outside his circle of friends when he…

franz-anton-von-kolowrat-liebsteinsky.s: Franz Anton von Kolowrat-Liebsteinsky was a Bohemian noble and Austrian statesman who directed internal and financial affairs from 1826. Under the incapable Emperor Ferdinand I he sat with Metternich in the State Conference that governed the empire, and their rivalry helped…

firishta.s: Firishta, Muhammad Qasim Hindu Shah, was a Persian historian born in Astarabad who served the Nizam Shahi court at Ahmadnagar and then Ibrahim Adil Shah II at Bijapur. His Tarikh-i Firishta, completed in the early seventeenth century, is a history of Muslim rule in India and…

firuz-shah-bahmani.s: Taj ud-Din Firuz Shah was sultan of the Bahmani Sultanate from 1397 to 1422. A learned ruler, he encouraged Persian scholars and built the palace city of Firuzabad on the Bhima river.

francis-peirson.s: Francis Peirson was a British army officer who commanded the troops in Jersey when a French force under Philippe de Rullecourt seized Saint Helier on 6 January 1781. Disregarding the surrender signed by the lieutenant-governor, the 24-year-old major led regulars and militia…

francois-coillard.s: François Coillard was a French Protestant missionary of the Paris Evangelical Missionary Society. After two decades in Lesotho he travelled north and in 1886 began a mission among the Lozi of Barotseland, founding stations at Sefula and Lealui.

fortress-of-humaita.s: The Fortress of Humaitá was a Paraguayan fortification on a bend of the Paraguay River near its junction with the Paraná, guarding the river route to Asunción. During the Paraguayan War it held back the allied forces of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay for years, until Brazilian…

francisco-de-sande.s: Francisco de Sande was a Spanish lawyer and colonial official who served as governor-general of the Philippines from 1575 to 1580. In 1578 he led an expedition against the Sultanate of Brunei, starting the Castilian War, and briefly captured its capital before disease forced…

fitna-of-al-andalus.s: The Fitna of al-Andalus was the civil war that destroyed the Caliphate of Córdoba between 1009 and 1031. It began with a revolt against the Amirid regime and pitted rival Umayyad claimants, Berber troops, Saqaliba commanders and the Hammudids against one another, while Córdoba…

frederick-banting.s: Frederick Banting was a Canadian physician who, with Charles Best and colleagues at the University of Toronto, isolated insulin in 1921–1922, turning diabetes from a fatal disease into a treatable one. He and J. J. R. Macleod received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine…

front-de-liberation-du-quebec.s: The Front de libération du Québec was a militant separatist group that sought Quebec independence through armed action. From 1963 it carried out bombings in Montreal and elsewhere.

felix-manz.s: Felix Manz was a Swiss Anabaptist leader from Zürich and a former follower of Zwingli. With Conrad Grebel and George Blaurock he took part in the first adult baptisms in January 1525.

first-war-of-villmergen.s: The First War of Villmergen was a brief religious war in the Old Swiss Confederacy in 1656 between the Protestant cantons of Zürich and Bern and the Catholic cantons. It arose from the expulsion of Protestants from Schwyz.

felix-and-regula.s: Felix and Regula are the patron saints of Zürich, a brother and sister said by legend to have been soldiers of the Theban Legion who fled to Zürich and were beheaded there for their Christian faith around 300. Their cult developed in the Carolingian period around the…

first-mithridatic-war.s: The First Mithridatic War was fought from 89 to 85 BCE between Rome and Mithridates VI of Pontus. Mithridates overran Roman Asia, ordered the massacre of Romans and Italians there in 88 BCE and won over many Greek cities, including Athens.

francis-dhanis.s: Francis Dhanis was a Belgian officer of the Congo Free State who commanded its forces in the Congo Arab war of 1892–1894, taking Nyangwe and Kasongo. In 1896 he led a large expedition towards the Nile, which collapsed in 1897 when its Tetela soldiers mutinied.

ferdinand-count-of-flanders.s: Ferdinand, known as Ferrand, was a Portuguese prince, son of King Sancho I, who became count of Flanders and Hainaut by marrying Countess Joan in 1212. He joined the coalition of Otto IV and King John of England against Philip II Augustus and was captured at the Battle of…

four-members-of-flanders.s: The Four Members of Flanders were the bodies that spoke for the County of Flanders in its dealings with its rulers: the great cities of Ghent, Bruges and Ypres, joined in the fourteenth century by the rural district of the Franc of Bruges. They negotiated taxation, trade and…

franc-of-bruges.s: The Franc of Bruges was the rural castellany surrounding Bruges in the County of Flanders, which governed itself through its own aldermen. Prosperous and populous, it was recognised in the fourteenth century as the fourth of the Four Members of Flanders, alongside Ghent,…

french-flanders.s: French Flanders is the part of the historical County of Flanders that belongs to France, in today's Nord department, around Lille, Douai, Dunkirk and Hazebrouck. It was won by France in the seventeenth century: Dunkirk was bought from England in 1662, and Louis XIV's conquests…

french-hainaut.s: French Hainaut is the southern part of the old County of Hainaut annexed by France in the seventeenth century, through the Treaty of the Pyrenees of 1659 and the Treaty of Nijmegen of 1678. It included Valenciennes, Maubeuge, Condé, Le Quesnoy, Landrecies and Avesnes, was…

frederick-i-burgrave-of-nuremberg.s: Frederick I was a count of Zollern, as Frederick III, who became burgrave of Nuremberg around 1192 through his marriage to Sophia of Raabs, heiress of the previous burgraves. A loyal follower of the Staufer emperors, he founded the Franconian line of the Hohenzollerns: his…

frederick-william-iv-of-prussia.s: Frederick William IV was king of Prussia from 1840 to 1861. A romantic conservative who admired the Middle Ages, he was forced by the revolution of 1848 to grant a constitution, but in 1849 refused the imperial crown offered by the Frankfurt Parliament.

fourth-council-of-the-lateran.s: The Fourth Council of the Lateran was held in Rome in November 1215 under Pope Innocent III. The largest church council of the Middle Ages, it defined transubstantiation, required annual confession, ordered Jews and Muslims to wear distinctive dress and planned a new crusade.

fredelo.s: Fredelo was a Frankish count of Toulouse in the mid-ninth century. He held the city for Pepin II of Aquitaine before handing it over to King Charles the Bald in 849, who confirmed him as count.

feodosia.s: Feodosia is a port city on the south-east coast of Crimea. Founded as the Greek colony of Theodosia in the sixth century BCE, it became Caffa, the main Genoese trading colony on the Black Sea from the late thirteenth century and a great market for grain and slaves.

furs-of-valencia.s: The Furs of Valencia were the law code of the Kingdom of Valencia, which James I of Aragon swore as the realm's general law in 1261. Based largely on Roman law and later written in Catalan, they were extended by later kings and the Valencian Corts.

francisco-jimenez-de-cisneros.s: Francisco Jiménez de Cisneros was a Franciscan friar who became confessor to Isabella I, Archbishop of Toledo in 1495, cardinal and Inquisitor General. He reformed the Castilian clergy, pressed the forced conversion of the Muslims of Granada and twice acted as regent of Castile.

francisco-gomez-de-sandoval-duke-of-lerm.n: Francisco Gómez de Sandoval, Duke of Lerma
francisco-gomez-de-sandoval-duke-of-lerm.s: Francisco Gómez de Sandoval, Duke of Lerma, was the favourite, or valido, of Philip III of Spain, who governed in his name from 1598 to 1618. His government made the Twelve Years' Truce with the Dutch, began the expulsion of the Moriscos in 1609 and moved the court to…

frederick-i-of-denmark.s: Frederick I was king of Denmark from 1523 and of Norway from 1524 until 1533, a younger son of Christian I and duke of Schleswig-Holstein. The Danish nobility elected him after deposing his nephew Christian II.

flemish-baroque-painting.s: Flemish Baroque painting is the art of the Southern Netherlands from the late sixteenth to the late seventeenth century, centred on Antwerp. flemish-brabant.s: Flemish Brabant is a province of Belgium in the Flemish Region, created in 1995 when the old province of Brabant was divided along the language border. Its capital is Leuven, and it surrounds the Brussels-Capital Region.

fougeres.s: Fougères is a town in the Ille-et-Vilaine department of north-eastern Brittany. Its castle, one of the largest medieval fortresses in Europe, guarded the Breton border with Normandy and Maine.

francis-iii-duke-of-brittany.s: Francis III was duke of Brittany from 1524 to 1536, the eldest son of Francis I of France and Claude of France, known as the Dauphin Francis. He was crowned duke at Rennes in 1532, the year the Estates of Brittany agreed to union with France.

first-treaty-of-guerande.s: The First Treaty of Guérande, signed on 12 April 1365, ended the War of the Breton Succession after the death of Charles of Blois at Auray. fontaine-les-dijon.s: Fontaine-lès-Dijon is a small town just north of Dijon in the Côte-d'Or department of Burgundy. It is the birthplace of Bernard of Clairvaux, born there in 1090 in the castle of his father, the knight Tescelin, and the site of his family home has long been a place of…

filarete.s: Filarete, born Antonio di Pietro Averlino, was a Florentine sculptor and architect. He cast the bronze doors of Old St Peter's Basilica in Rome and from 1451 worked in Milan for Francesco Sforza, designing the Ospedale Maggiore and working on the Sforza Castle.

francesco-bussone-da-carmagnola.s: Francesco Bussone, called Carmagnola after his birthplace in Piedmont, was a condottiere who reconquered much of Lombardy for Filippo Maria Visconti, duke of Milan. After falling out with the duke he entered Venetian service in 1425 and defeated the Milanese at Maclodio in 1427.

francesco-ii-sforza.s: Francesco II Sforza was the last Sforza duke of Milan, a son of Ludovico Sforza. Restored to the duchy in 1521 by Charles V after the French were driven out, he ruled under imperial protection during the Italian Wars and was briefly deposed after joining the League of Cognac…

falaise.s: Falaise is a town in the Calvados department of Normandy, dominated by a castle on a rocky outcrop above the Ante valley. It was a residence of the dukes of Normandy and the birthplace of William the Conqueror around 1028.

francesco-farnese-duke-of-parma.s: Francesco Farnese was duke of Parma and Piacenza from 1694 to 1727. fritzlar.s: Fritzlar is a town in northern Hesse, Germany, on the Eder river. Saint Boniface founded a church and monastery there after felling the sacred Donar's Oak nearby in 723, and it became a centre of the Christian mission in Hesse.

foreign-orientals.s: Foreign Orientals (Vreemde Oosterlingen) was a legal category in the Dutch East Indies for residents of Asian origin who were neither Europeans nor natives, chiefly Chinese, Arabs and Indians. The classification subjected them to separate rules on law, residence, travel and…

first-stadtholderless-period.s: The First Stadtholderless Period was the era from 1650 to 1672 when the leading provinces of the Dutch Republic left the office of stadtholder vacant after the death of William II of Orange. franco-dutch-war.s: The Franco-Dutch War was fought from 1672 to 1678 between France and its allies and the Dutch Republic, later supported by Spain, Brandenburg and the Holy Roman Emperor. Louis XIV's invasion in 1672 nearly destroyed the Republic, which survived by flooding the Holland Water Line.

frans-hals.s: Frans Hals was a Dutch painter of Haarlem, one of the great portraitists of the Dutch Golden Age. Born in Antwerp, he was known for loose, rapid brushwork that gave his sitters a lively, spontaneous air, as in The Laughing Cavalier and his large group portraits of Haarlem…

frederick-henry-prince-of-orange.s: Frederick Henry, Prince of Orange, was stadtholder of most provinces of the Dutch Republic from 1625 to 1647. frederick-william-ii-of-prussia.s: Frederick William II was King of Prussia from 1786 to 1797, nephew and successor of Frederick the Great. In 1787 he sent an army into the Dutch Republic to restore the authority of Stadtholder William V, husband of his sister Wilhelmina, against the Patriots.

fiyanggu.s: Fiyanggu was a Manchu general of the Qing dynasty. During the Kangxi Emperor's campaign of 1696 against the Dzungar ruler Galdan, he led the western column across the Gobi and destroyed Galdan's army at the Battle of Jao Modo near the Tuul River.

frankenthal.s: Frankenthal is a town in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, between Worms and Ludwigshafen. In 1562 Elector Frederick III settled Calvinist refugees from the Netherlands there, and their community of Flemish and Walloon craftsmen made it a centre of tapestry weaving and, later, of…

formula-of-concord.s: The Formula of Concord is a Lutheran confession of faith completed in 1577 to settle the doctrinal disputes that followed Martin Luther's death. Drafted chiefly by Jakob Andreae and Martin Chemnitz with the support of Elector Augustus of Saxony, it was published with earlier…

frederick-christian-elector-of-saxony.s: Frederick Christian was Elector of Saxony for about ten weeks in 1763, succeeding his father Augustus III after the Seven Years' War. freiberg-mining-academy.s: The Freiberg Mining Academy (Bergakademie Freiberg) was founded in 1765 in the silver-mining town of Freiberg in Saxony, as part of the reconstruction after the Seven Years' War, and is the oldest university of mining and metallurgy still in operation. first-mexican-empire.s: The First Mexican Empire was the monarchy established after Mexico won independence from Spain in 1821, with Agustín de Iturbide crowned as Emperor Agustín I in 1822. felix-mendelssohn.s: Felix Mendelssohn (1809–1847) was a German composer, pianist and conductor born in Hamburg, the grandson of the philosopher Moses Mendelssohn. His works include the overture to A Midsummer Night's Dream, the Italian and Scottish symphonies, the oratorio Elijah and the Violin…

ferhat-abbas.s: Ferhat Abbas (1899–1985) was an Algerian nationalist politician and pharmacist from Sétif. At first an advocate of equal rights within France, he issued the Manifesto of the Algerian People in 1943 calling for an autonomous Algeria, and in 1956 he joined the FLN.

financial-delegations.s: The Financial Delegations were an elected assembly created in Algeria in 1898 to vote the colony's budget, which became separate from France's in 1900. frantz-fanon.s: Frantz Fanon (1925–1961) was a psychiatrist and political philosopher from Martinique. While head of a psychiatric ward at Blida in Algeria he joined the FLN, and he became a leading voice of the Algerian revolution.

franco-siamese-war.s: The Franco-Siamese War was a brief conflict in 1893 between France and the Kingdom of Siam over the Lao lands east of the Mekong. After French gunboats forced their way up the Chao Phraya to Bangkok in the Paknam incident in July, Siam accepted a treaty in October ceding the…

franco-thai-war.s: The Franco-Thai War was fought between Thailand and Vichy French Indochina from late 1940 to early 1941 over territories that Siam had ceded to France decades earlier. The French navy won at Ko Chang in January 1941, but Japan imposed a settlement, confirmed by a treaty in…

fazughli.s: Fazughli is a region on the Blue Nile in south-eastern Sudan, near the border with Ethiopia. It was a frontier province of the Funj Sultanate of Sennar and an important source of gold, which was traded north to Egypt.

funj-chronicle.s: The Funj Chronicle is a history of the Funj Sultanate of Sennar and the early Turco-Egyptian period in the Sudan, compiled in Arabic in the nineteenth century and attributed in its original form to Ahmad Katib al-Shuna. It survives in several recensions and provides the…

final-act-of-the-congress-of-vienna.n: Final Act of the Congress of Vienna
final-act-of-the-congress-of-vienna.s: The Final Act of the Congress of Vienna, signed on 9 June 1815, brought together the agreements reached by the European powers at the Congress of Vienna into a single treaty. frankfurt-congress-of-princes.s: The Frankfurt Congress of Princes was a meeting of German sovereigns convened by Emperor Franz Joseph of Austria in Frankfurt in August 1863 to approve an Austrian plan for reforming the German Confederation. farrukhi-sistani.s: Farrukhi Sistani was a Persian poet from Sistan who served at the court of Mahmud of Ghazni and his son Mas'ud I. He is known for his panegyric odes celebrating the Ghaznavid sultans and their campaigns, including the expedition to Somnath, written in a clear and graceful…

friday-mosque-of-herat.s: The Friday Mosque of Herat is the principal congregational mosque of Herat in western Afghanistan. An earlier mosque on the site was rebuilt by the Ghurid sultan Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad around 1200, and a Ghurid portal survives.

former-yan.s: Former Yan was a state of the Xianbei Murong clan in north-eastern China, proclaimed by Murong Huang in 337 during the Sixteen Kingdoms period. In 342 it sacked the Goguryeo capital and carried off the queen mother and the body of the previous king.

first-sea-lord.s: The First Sea Lord is the professional head of the British Royal Navy and the senior naval officer on the Admiralty Board. Holders have included John Fisher, who led the navy's modernisation before the First World War, and Prince Louis of Battenberg, who resigned in 1914 amid…

friedrich-ludwig-weidig.s: Friedrich Ludwig Weidig was a Protestant pastor and schoolteacher in the Grand Duchy of Hesse and a leading figure of the liberal and democratic opposition. In 1834 he edited and helped distribute Georg Büchner's revolutionary pamphlet Der Hessische Landbote.

frankfurt-rhine-main.s: Frankfurt Rhine-Main is a metropolitan region of western Germany around the confluence of the Rhine and Main, including Frankfurt, Wiesbaden, Mainz, Darmstadt and Offenbach. With about six million inhabitants it is one of Germany's main economic areas, home to banking,…

francysk-skaryna.s: Francysk Skaryna was a printer, translator and physician from Polotsk in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. In 1517-1519 he printed books of the Bible in Prague in a Church Slavonic close to the vernacular, and in the 1520s he set up the first printing press in Vilnius.

fortress-of-luxembourg.s: The Fortress of Luxembourg was the fortified city of Luxembourg, strengthened over centuries by Burgundian, Spanish, French, Austrian and Prussian rulers until it was called the 'Gibraltar of the North'. After 1815 it was a federal fortress of the German Confederation held by…

florentine-camerata.s: The Florentine Camerata was a circle of humanists, poets and musicians who met in Florence in the 1570s and 1580s, chiefly at the house of Count Giovanni de' Bardi. Members such as Vincenzo Galilei and Giulio Caccini sought to revive the expressive power of ancient Greek drama…

forte-di-belvedere.s: The Forte di Belvedere is a fortress on the Boboli hill above Florence, built in 1590–1595 for Grand Duke Ferdinando I de' Medici to designs attributed to Bernardo Buontalenti. Overlooking the Pitti Palace and the city, it was meant both to defend Florence and to secure the…

friedrich-wilhelm-von-haugwitz.s: Friedrich Wilhelm von Haugwitz was a Saxon-born statesman and the chief architect of Maria Theresa's administrative reforms after the loss of Silesia. francisco-de-quevedo.s: Francisco de Quevedo was a Spanish poet, satirist and prose writer of the Golden Age. Known for brilliant conceptist wordplay, he wrote the picaresque novel El Buscón, the satirical Sueños and a large body of poetry, and he feuded bitterly with Luis de Góngora.

francisco-de-zurbaran.s: Francisco de Zurbarán was a Spanish Baroque painter, active mainly in Seville. He is best known for austere religious paintings of monks, saints and martyrs, painted for monasteries with strong contrasts of light and shadow, and for a few still lifes of great simplicity.

flavius-asturius.s: Flavius Asturius was a Western Roman general who, as commander of both services, was sent to Hispania Tarraconensis in 441 to suppress the Bagaudae, the rural rebels of the Ebro valley. He was succeeded in the command by his son-in-law, the poet Merobaudes, and held the…

fructuosus-of-tarragona.s: Fructuosus was bishop of Tarraco, the capital of Hispania Tarraconensis, and a Christian martyr. During the persecution under the emperor Valerian he was burned alive with his deacons Augurius and Eulogius in the city's amphitheatre in January 259.

felipe-guaman-poma-de-ayala.s: Felipe Guaman Poma de Ayala was an Andean nobleman of Peru who wrote the Nueva corónica y buen gobierno, a chronicle of about 1,200 pages addressed to the king of Spain around 1615. first-bulgarian-empire.s: The First Bulgarian Empire was a medieval state founded around 681 by the Bulgar khan Asparukh on the lower Danube. fueros-de-aragon.s: The Fueros de Aragón are the compilation of the customary laws of the Kingdom of Aragon made at the Cortes of Huesca in 1247 under James I, prepared by Bishop Vidal de Canellas of Huesca. Replacing a variety of local laws, they became the general law of the kingdom, extended…

favila-of-asturias.s: Favila was king of Asturias from 737 to 739, succeeding his father Pelagius. According to the Asturian chronicles he was killed by a bear while hunting, after only two years on the throne.

fruela-i-of-asturias.s: Fruela I was king of Asturias from 757 to 768, the son of Alfonso I and Ermesinda. He fought the Muslims of al-Andalus and put down revolts in Galicia and among the Basques, and married the Basque captive Munia, mother of Alfonso II.

franz-marc.s: Franz Marc was a German painter and a leading figure of German Expressionism. With Wassily Kandinsky he founded the Blue Rider group in Munich in 1911.

friedrich-von-gartner.s: Friedrich von Gärtner was a German architect who worked for Ludwig I of Bavaria. He completed the Ludwigstrasse in Munich in a round-arched, Romanesque-inspired style, building the Bavarian State Library, the Ludwigskirche, the university, the Feldherrnhalle and the Siegestor.

furth.s: Fürth is a city in Middle Franconia, Bavaria, adjoining Nuremberg. Long a market town with one of the largest Jewish communities in southern Germany, it grew into an industrial city in the nineteenth century.

frantisek-palacky.s: František Palacký was a Czech historian and politician, called the "father of the nation". His multi-volume "History of the Czech Nation in Bohemia and Moravia" presented the Hussite era as the high point of Czech history.

first-franco-dahomean-war.s: The First Franco-Dahomean War was fought in 1890 between France and the Kingdom of Dahomey under King Behanzin, over French claims to Cotonou and protection of Porto-Novo. Dahomean forces, including the women soldiers, attacked French positions at Cotonou and Atchoupa.

francisco-felix-de-souza.s: Francisco Félix de Souza was a Brazilian slave trader who became the most powerful merchant at Ouidah, the main port of the Kingdom of Dahomey. fyrkat.s: Fyrkat is a Viking-age ring fortress near Hobro in northern Jutland, Denmark, built around 980, probably under Harald Bluetooth. Its circular rampart, about 120 metres across, enclosed sixteen longhouses arranged in four squares.

folketing.s: The Folketing is the parliament of Denmark. Created by the constitution of 1849 as the lower chamber of the Rigsdag, it became the only chamber in 1953.

frederik-x.s: Frederik X is King of Denmark, who succeeded on 14 January 2024 when his mother, Queen Margrethe II, abdicated. Before his accession he served for decades as crown prince, trained in the armed forces and studied political science.

francois-ravaillac.s: François Ravaillac was a French Catholic zealot who assassinated King Henry IV of France in Paris on 14 May 1610, stabbing him while his coach was stopped in the rue de la Ferronnerie. He believed the king, a former Protestant, meant to make war on the pope.

flight-to-varennes.s: The Flight to Varennes was the attempted escape of King Louis XVI, Marie Antoinette and their children from Paris on the night of 20–21 June 1791. Hoping to reach royalist troops near the eastern frontier, they were recognised and stopped at Varennes-en-Argonne and brought…

fifth-crusade.s: The Fifth Crusade was a campaign of 1217–1221 to recover Jerusalem by attacking Ayyubid power in Egypt. Andrew II of Hungary and Leopold VI of Austria led the first contingents to Acre in 1217, but Andrew soon returned home.

first-anglo-mysore-war.s: The First Anglo-Mysore War (1767–1769) was fought between Hyder Ali's Mysore and the British East India Company, with the Nizam of Hyderabad and the Marathas drawn in at different stages. fabrizio-ruffo.s: Fabrizio Ruffo (1744–1827) was a Neapolitan cardinal and politician. In 1799 he landed in Calabria with a handful of followers and raised the Army of the Holy Faith, which overthrew the Parthenopean Republic and restored Ferdinand IV.

first-carlist-war.s: The First Carlist War (1833–1840) was a Spanish civil war over the succession to Ferdinand VII. Supporters of his brother Carlos, strongest in the Basque provinces, Navarre and Catalonia, fought for him and for traditional rights against the liberal regency of Maria Christina…

foral-community-of-navarre.s: The Foral Community of Navarre is an autonomous community of northern Spain with its capital at Pamplona. fridtjof-nansen.s: Fridtjof Nansen (1861–1930) was a Norwegian explorer, scientist and humanitarian. He made the first crossing of the Greenland ice cap in 1888 and drifted across the Arctic Ocean in the Fram in 1893–1896.

frostating.s: The Frostating was the medieval law assembly for Trøndelag in central Norway, meeting on the Frosta peninsula in the Trondheimsfjord. Its law code, the Frostating Law, traditionally associated with Haakon the Good, is one of the main sources for early Norwegian law.

forteviot.s: Forteviot is a village in Strathearn, Perthshire, Scotland, that was a royal centre of the Pictish and early Scottish kings. The Pictish king Constantín son of Fergus is commemorated on the nearby Dupplin Cross, and Kenneth mac Alpin died at the royal residence there in 858.

ferdinand-christian-baur.s: Ferdinand Christian Baur was a German Protestant theologian, professor at Tübingen from 1826 and founder of the Tübingen school of biblical criticism. frederick-ii-elector-of-brandenburg.s: Frederick II, called Irontooth, was Elector of Brandenburg from 1440 to 1470, son of Frederick I. He broke the independence of the twin towns of Berlin and Cölln in 1448 and began a castle on the Spree that became the Hohenzollern residence.

friedrich-wilhelm-canal.s: The Friedrich-Wilhelm Canal is a canal in Brandenburg, Germany, built in 1662–1668 under the Great Elector Frederick William. Running from the Spree near Müllrose to the Oder, it linked the river systems of the Elbe and the Oder for the first time and drew trade between…

francisco-i-madero.s: Francisco I. Madero was a Mexican landowner and politician who challenged Porfirio Díaz in the 1910 election and, after his arrest, called for revolt in the Plan of San Luis Potosí, beginning the Mexican Revolution.

first-cataract.s: The First Cataract is the stretch of rapids and granite islands on the Nile at Aswan, the northernmost of the river's cataracts. For much of antiquity it marked the southern frontier of Egypt with Nubia, and its quarries supplied granite for monuments.

fatehpur-sikri.s: Fatehpur Sikri is a city near Agra in Uttar Pradesh, India, founded by the Mughal emperor Akbar near the shrine of the Sufi saint Salim Chishti and his capital from 1571 to 1585. Built of red sandstone, its palaces, Jama Masjid and the Buland Darwaza combine Persian and Indian…

francisco-barreto.s: Francisco Barreto was a Portuguese soldier and administrator who governed Portuguese India from 1555 to 1558. In 1569 he was sent to lead a large expedition up the Zambezi to conquer the gold mines of the Mutapa kingdom.

flensburg.s: Flensburg is a port city in Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, at the head of the Flensburg Fjord close to the Danish border. Part of the Danish realm for centuries, it passed to Prussia in 1864 and remained German after the plebiscite of 1920.

francois-gaston-de-levis.s: François-Gaston de Lévis was a French general who served as Montcalm's second-in-command in New France during the Seven Years' War. fort-duquesne.s: Fort Duquesne was a French fort built in 1754 at the forks of the Ohio River, where the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers meet, on the site of present-day Pittsburgh. Its seizure from Virginian builders helped start the French and Indian War.

fort-frontenac.s: Fort Frontenac was a French fort founded in 1673 by Governor Frontenac where Lake Ontario flows into the St Lawrence, on the site of present-day Kingston, Ontario. A base for the fur trade and for campaigns against the Iroquois, it was captured and destroyed by a British force…

fort-niagara.s: Fort Niagara is a fortress at the mouth of the Niagara River on Lake Ontario, in present-day New York State. The French built a stone 'French Castle' there in 1726 to control the route to the upper Great Lakes.

fort-oswego.s: Fort Oswego was a British trading post and fort built in the 1720s at the mouth of the Oswego River on Lake Ontario, in present-day New York State, to compete with the French for the fur trade of the Great Lakes. In August 1756 the Marquis de Montcalm besieged and captured it…

felix-maria-calleja.s: Félix María Calleja was a Spanish army officer who led royalist forces against the Mexican insurgents from 1810. He defeated Miguel Hidalgo's much larger army at the Bridge of Calderón in January 1811 and besieged José María Morelos at Cuautla in 1812.

fernando-pereira.s: Fernando Pereira was a Portuguese-born Dutch photographer working for Greenpeace. He was killed on 10 July 1985 when agents of the French foreign intelligence service sank the Greenpeace ship Rainbow Warrior with two bombs in Auckland harbour, New Zealand, before it could sail…

foreshore-and-seabed-act-2004.s: The Foreshore and Seabed Act 2004 was a New Zealand law that vested ownership of the public foreshore and seabed in the Crown, after a Court of Appeal ruling in 2003 had opened the way for Māori customary title claims. francis-garnier.s: Francis Garnier was a French naval officer and explorer. He led the Mekong exploration expedition of 1866–1868 after the death of its commander, Ernest Doudart de Lagrée, showing that the river was not a navigable route to China.

frederic-cesar-de-la-harpe.s: Frédéric-César de La Harpe was a Swiss political leader from Vaud and tutor to the future Tsar Alexander I of Russia. francis-william-reitz.s: Francis William Reitz was a lawyer, politician and poet who served as president of the Orange Free State from 1889 until ill health forced his resignation in 1895. He then became state secretary of the South African Republic and supported the Boer cause in the Second Boer War.

fontainebleau.s: Fontainebleau is a town south-east of Paris, France, surrounded by a large forest and known for its royal palace, rebuilt by Francis I in the sixteenth century and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Napoleon held Pope Pius VII there from 1812 to 1814, extracting the short-lived…

fausto-sozzini.s: Fausto Sozzini was an Italian theologian from Siena whose Antitrinitarian teaching gave its name to Socinianism. He settled in Poland in 1579 and became the leading thinker of the Polish Brethren, whose Racovian Catechism, published at Raków in 1605, reflected his rational…

ferdinand-of-bavaria-archbishop-of-colog.s: Ferdinand of Bavaria was a Wittelsbach prince who was archbishop-elector of Cologne and prince-bishop of Liège from 1612 until 1650, as well as bishop of several other sees. A leading figure of the Catholic Reformation, he fought the Grignoux faction in Liège and imposed his…

francois-charles-de-velbruck.s: François-Charles de Velbruck was prince-bishop of Liège from 1772 to 1784. An enlightened ruler, he promoted education, public health, poor relief and the arts, and supported the founding of the Société libre d'Émulation in 1779.

ferdinand-of-majorca.s: Ferdinand of Majorca was a prince of the Majorcan branch of the house of Barcelona who briefly led the Catalan Company in Greece. He married Isabella of Sabran, heiress to Achaea, and in 1315 invaded the Peloponnese to claim the principality for their son James, but was…

florent-of-hainaut.s: Florent of Hainaut was a Flemish nobleman who became prince of Achaea in 1289 by marrying Isabella of Villehardouin. He made a truce with the Byzantines that brought several years of peace and prosperity to the principality, and he was the father of Matilda of Hainaut.

frankokratia.s: Frankokratia ('rule of the Franks') is the period of Western, chiefly French and Italian, rule in Greek lands after the Fourth Crusade of 1204. It covered the Principality of Achaea, the Duchy of Athens, Venetian colonies and other Latin states; most were lost to the…

front-palace.s: The Front Palace, or Wang Na, was the residence and office of the uparat, the viceroy or 'second king' of the Siamese court, and by extension the office itself. In Bangkok it stood north of the Grand Palace, and its holder commanded his own officials and troops.

four-asian-tigers.s: The Four Asian Tigers are Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea and Taiwan, economies that industrialised rapidly from the 1960s to the 1990s. Through export-led manufacturing, high savings and investment in education, they moved from poverty to high incomes within a generation.

fernando-villavicencio.s: Fernando Villavicencio was an Ecuadorian investigative journalist and politician who exposed corruption in the oil sector and under the government of Rafael Correa. As a member of the National Assembly and presidential candidate in 2023, he campaigned against organised crime.

farabundo-marti.s: Agustín Farabundo Martí was a Salvadoran communist leader who had served as secretary to Augusto César Sandino in Nicaragua. He helped organise the peasant and indigenous uprising of January 1932 in western El Salvador but was arrested before it broke out and executed by…

farabundo-marti-national-liberation-fron.s: The Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front (FMLN) was formed in October 1980 as a coalition of five Salvadoran left-wing guerrilla organisations and named after the communist leader Farabundo Martí. It fought the government in the civil war of 1980–1992, which ended with…

francisco-duenas.s: Francisco Dueñas was a conservative Salvadoran politician who held the presidency several times between 1851 and 1871. Backed by the Guatemalan dictator Rafael Carrera, who overthrew Gerardo Barrios in 1863, he ruled from 1863 to 1871.

federal-republic-of-central-america.s: The Federal Republic of Central America was a federation of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica, formed after independence from Spain and the end of union with Mexico in 1823. Torn by conflict between liberals and conservatives, it was led for most of…

finnish-civil-war.s: The Finnish Civil War was fought from January to May 1918, shortly after Finland's independence, between the socialist Reds, strongest in the industrial south, and the government's Whites under Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim. With the help of German troops, the Whites won.

finlandisation.s: Finlandisation is the term, coined in West German debates of the 1960s and 1970s, for the policy by which Finland kept its democracy and market economy after 1944 while avoiding anything that might provoke the Soviet Union. Rooted in the treaty of 1948 and practised by…

finno-soviet-treaty-of-1948.s: The Finno-Soviet Treaty of 1948, formally the Agreement of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance, was signed in Moscow on 6 April 1948. Finland undertook to resist any attack by Germany or its allies on itself, or on the Soviet Union through Finnish territory, while…

filippo-brunelleschi.s: Filippo Brunelleschi (1377–1446) was a Florentine architect and engineer, regarded as a founder of Renaissance architecture. florentine-catasto.s: The Florentine Catasto of 1427 was a tax survey introduced by the Republic of Florence, which required every household in the city and its territory to declare its members, property, investments and debts. Designed to spread the burden of war taxation more fairly, it produced…

farinata-degli-uberti.s: Farinata degli Uberti (c. 1212–1264) was a Florentine nobleman and leader of the city's Ghibelline faction. Exiled in 1258, he helped lead the Ghibelline forces that crushed the Guelphs at Montaperti in 1260, and at the council of Empoli that followed he alone opposed the…

florence-cathedral.s: Florence Cathedral, the Cattedrale di Santa Maria del Fiore, is the cathedral of Florence, begun in 1296 to designs by Arnolfo di Cambio and consecrated in 1436. Its octagonal dome by Filippo Brunelleschi, completed in 1436, was the largest built since antiquity, and with…

francesco-ferrucci.s: Francesco Ferrucci (1489–1530) was a Florentine military commander during the siege of Florence in 1529–1530, when the last republic resisted the imperial and papal armies restoring the Medici. Leading a relief army from Volterra and Pisa, he was defeated and captured at…

francesco-guicciardini.s: Francesco Guicciardini (1483–1540) was a Florentine historian, diplomat and statesman. He served as ambassador to Spain, as papal governor of Modena, Reggio and the Romagna and as an adviser to the first Medici duke, and he was a friend and critic of Machiavelli.

fernand-braudel.s: Fernand Braudel (1902–1985) was a French historian and leading figure of the Annales school. His The Mediterranean and the Mediterranean World in the Age of Philip II (1949) studied history at the levels of geography, slow economic and social structures, and events, and his…

federico-ponce-vaides.s: Federico Ponce Vaides (1889–1956) was a Guatemalan general who became provisional president in July 1944 after protests forced the dictator Jorge Ubico to resign. When he tried to keep power through a managed election, a revolt by young officers, students and workers overthrew…

francisco-ferrera.s: Francisco Ferrera (1794–1851) was a Honduran general and the first president of Honduras as a separate state after the break-up of the Federal Republic of Central America, serving from 1841 to 1845. A conservative allied with Rafael Carrera of Guatemala, he fought the…

forest-brothers.s: The Forest Brothers were partisans who waged guerrilla war against Soviet rule in Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia after the Red Army's return in 1944. Strongest in Lithuania, where tens of thousands fought, they hoped for a Western intervention that never came.

fruto-chamorro.s: Fruto Chamorro was a Nicaraguan Conservative politician from Granada who became supreme director of Nicaragua in 1853 and, under the constitution of 1854, its first president. His rule provoked a Liberal revolt from León in 1854, which drew in the American filibuster William…

ferdinand-de-lesseps.s: Ferdinand de Lesseps was a French diplomat and entrepreneur who developed the Suez Canal, opened in 1869. Encouraged by that success, he launched a French company to build a sea-level canal across Panama in 1881, but disease, landslides and engineering problems overwhelmed the…

fernando-belaunde-terry.s: Fernando Belaúnde Terry was a Peruvian architect and politician, founder of the Popular Action party, who was president of Peru from 1963 to 1968 and from 1980 to 1985. His first government, which promoted roads and settlement in the Amazon, was overthrown by General Juan…

fort-lovrijenac.s: Fort Lovrijenac (St Lawrence) is a fortress standing on a sea cliff 37 metres high just outside the western walls of Dubrovnik. Built in the Middle Ages and strengthened in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, it guarded the city's western approaches by land and sea against…

fort-revelin.s: Fort Revelin is a fortress outside the eastern land gate of Dubrovnik's walls, built in 1462–1463 when the Ottoman threat grew and rebuilt and greatly strengthened in 1538–1549 to plans by Antonio Ferramolino. It protected the Ploče gate and the eastern approach to the city.

fondaco-dei-tedeschi.s: The Fondaco dei Tedeschi is a large building beside the Rialto Bridge in Venice that served from the 13th century as the headquarters, warehouse and lodging of German merchants, who were required to live and trade there under Venetian supervision. After a fire it was rebuilt…

francesco-foscari.s: Francesco Foscari was Doge of Venice from 1423 to 1457, the longest reign of any doge. He led the republic into long wars against Milan that won Brescia and Bergamo and carried Venice's mainland frontier to the Adda.

faisal-bin-shamlan.s: Faisal bin Shamlan was a Yemeni engineer and politician from Hadramawt who served as oil minister and became known for his integrity, resigning from parliament in protest against an extension of its term. In 2006 he stood as the joint candidate of the opposition alliance…

fat-margaret.s: Fat Margaret is a massive round artillery tower guarding the Great Coastal Gate at the northern end of the old town of Tallinn (Reval). Built in the early 16th century, it is about 25 metres across, with walls up to about 5 metres thick, designed both to defend the harbour…

flavia-caesariensis.s: Flavia Caesariensis was one of the provinces created in Roman Britain by the reforms of Diocletian around 300. It probably covered eastern and central England, with its capital at Lindum (Lincoln).

fosse-way.s: The Fosse Way was a Roman road in Britain running about 370 kilometres from Exeter through Bath, Cirencester and Leicester to Lincoln. Built in the first decades after the conquest of 43 CE, it marked for a time the western limit of Roman control.

first-council-of-nicaea.s: The First Council of Nicaea was a gathering of Christian bishops called by the emperor Constantine I at Nicaea in Bithynia in 325. It condemned the teaching of Arius, adopted the Nicene Creed, which declared the Son to be of one substance with the Father, and set a common rule…

foedus-cassianum.s: The Foedus Cassianum was a treaty between Rome and the cities of the Latin League, traditionally dated to 493 BCE and named after the consul Spurius Cassius. Concluded after the Battle of Lake Regillus, it established peace and a defensive alliance in which both sides shared…

felix-dzerzhinsky.s: Felix Dzerzhinsky was a Polish-born Bolshevik revolutionary who founded and led the Cheka, the Soviet secret police, from December 1917. Under his direction it carried out the Red Terror against opponents during the Russian Civil War.

first-sho-dynasty.s: The First Shō dynasty ruled the kingdom of Chūzan and then a unified Ryukyu from 1406 to 1469. It was founded when Shō Hashi installed his father Shō Shishō as king, and it completed the unification of Okinawa in 1429.

feddersen-wierde.s: Feddersen Wierde is an excavated settlement mound near Bremerhaven in Lower Saxony, Germany, occupied from the first century BCE to the fifth century CE. Raised gradually against North Sea floods, it held longhouses that sheltered people and cattle under one roof, a…

falaki-shirvani.s: Falaki Shirvani was a Persian poet of the twelfth century from Shirvan, in present-day Azerbaijan. He served as a court poet of the Shirvanshah Manuchihr III, whose praises he sang in odes, and was a contemporary of Khaqani.

fariburz-i.s: Fariburz I was Shirvanshah, ruler of Shirvan in present-day Azerbaijan, in the second half of the eleventh century. During his reign the Seljuk Turks advanced into the Caucasus, and he accepted Seljuk overlordship and paid tribute to keep his throne.

first-boer-war.s: The First Boer War was a revolt of the Transvaal Boers against the British annexation of their republic in 1877. Beginning in December 1880, Boer commandos besieged British garrisons and defeated British columns at Laing's Nek and, decisively, at Majuba Hill on 27 February 1881.

five-year-plans-of-the-soviet-union.n: Five-year plans of the Soviet Union
five-year-plans-of-the-soviet-union.s: The five-year plans were the centralised economic plans by which the Soviet state directed production from 1928 until 1991. The First Five-Year Plan (1928–1932) and the Second (1933–1937) drove rapid heavy industrialisation, building steel works, power stations and new…

fan-ju.s: Fan Ju, also read Fan Sui, was a native of Wei who became chancellor of the State of Qin under King Zhaoxiang in 266 BCE. He advised Qin to ally with distant states while attacking its neighbours, a strategy that guided its later conquests.

first-peace-of-thorn.s: The First Peace of Thorn was signed at Toruń on 1 February 1411 between the Teutonic Order and the allied Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania, ending the war in which the Order was defeated at Grunwald. The Order lost little land beyond Samogitia, ceded for the…

fatahillah.s: Fatahillah was a Muslim commander in the service of the Sultanate of Demak who led the forces of Demak and Cirebon that took Banten and, in 1527, the Sunda port of Sunda Kalapa, defeating a Portuguese landing party. He renamed the port Jayakarta, and Jakarta dates its founding…

fort-nieuw-amsterdam.s: Fort Nieuw-Amsterdam is a pentagonal fortress built between 1734 and 1747 at the confluence of the Suriname and Commewijne rivers, opposite Paramaribo. It was built after the French raids of the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries to defend the plantation colony of…

fort-zeelandia-suriname.s: Fort Zeelandia is a fortress on the Suriname River at Paramaribo. Built by the English colonists of Willoughbyland, it was captured in February 1667 by a fleet from Zeeland under Abraham Crijnssen and renamed after that province.

francis-willoughby-5th-baron-willoughby-.n: Francis Willoughby, 5th Baron Willoughby of Parham
francis-willoughby-5th-baron-willoughby-.s: Francis Willoughby, 5th Baron Willoughby of Parham, was an English nobleman and royalist governor of Barbados. In 1650 he sent settlers from Barbados to the Suriname River, founding the colony known as Willoughbyland, which soon had several dozen sugar plantations worked by…

friedrich-durrenmatt.s: Friedrich Dürrenmatt was a Swiss playwright and novelist writing in German, one of the leading dramatists of the post-war period. frelimo.s: FRELIMO, the Mozambique Liberation Front, was founded in Dar es Salaam in June 1962 under Eduardo Mondlane by the union of exile nationalist groups. From bases in Tanzania it fought a guerrilla war against Portuguese rule from 1964 until Mozambique's independence in 1975, and…

force-intervention-brigade.s: The Force Intervention Brigade is a combat unit of the United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, authorised by the Security Council in March 2013 with a mandate to neutralise armed groups, the first UN force given such an offensive role. fifth-sun.s: In Aztec cosmology the Fifth Sun is the present age of the world, preceded by four earlier suns or eras each destroyed by catastrophe. According to the myth, the gods gathered at Teotihuacan, where the humble god Nanahuatzin threw himself into a fire and became the new sun,…

feodor-i-of-russia.s: Feodor I was tsar of Russia from 1584 to 1598, the son of Ivan IV and the last of the Rurikid line to rule Muscovy. Pious and withdrawn, he left government to his brother-in-law Boris Godunov, under whose regency the Moscow Patriarchate was established in 1589 and Russia…

feodor-iii-of-russia.s: Feodor III was tsar of Russia from 1676 to 1682, the eldest surviving son of Alexis. Educated by the scholar Simeon Polotsky and often ill, he ruled through favourites who carried out reforms, most notably the abolition in 1682 of mestnichestvo, the system that ranked nobles…

fred-rwigyema.s: Fred Rwigyema was a Rwandan Tutsi refugee raised in Uganda who fought with Yoweri Museveni's National Resistance Army in the Bush War and became deputy army commander and deputy minister of defence of Uganda. As leader of the Rwandan Patriotic Front he commanded its invasion…

freedom-charter.s: The Freedom Charter is the statement of principles adopted by the Congress of the People at Kliptown near Johannesburg on 26 June 1955, organised by the ANC and its allies in the Congress Alliance. Opening with the words 'South Africa belongs to all who live in it, black and…

factory-acts.s: The Factory Acts were a series of laws passed by the UK Parliament from 1802 onwards to regulate working conditions in industry. The Act of 1833 banned the employment of children under nine in textile mills and created the first factory inspectors, and later acts, such as the…

first-amendment-to-the-united-states-con.n: First Amendment to the United States Constitution
first-amendment-to-the-united-states-con.s: The First Amendment to the United States Constitution, ratified in 1791 as part of the Bill of Rights, forbids Congress to establish a religion or prohibit its free exercise, and protects freedom of speech, of the press, of peaceable assembly and of petition. As interpreted by…

franklin-d-roosevelt.s: Franklin D. Roosevelt was an American Democratic politician who served as the 32nd president of the United States from 1933 until his death in 1945, the only president elected four times. He answered the Great Depression with the New Deal and led the country through the Second…

first-dynasty-of-uruk.s: The First Dynasty of Uruk is the series of early kings of Uruk listed in the Sumerian King List, including Meskiaggasher, Enmerkar, Lugalbanda, Dumuzid and Gilgamesh. Its rulers, if historical, may have lived around the twenty-seventh century BCE and appear in Sumerian epics…

francisco-hernandez-giron.s: Francisco Hernández Girón was a Spanish conquistador who in November 1553 led the last major rebellion of the encomenderos in Peru, provoked by royal measures to abolish the forced personal service of indigenous people.
