feng-river.s: The Feng River is a southern tributary of the Wei River in Shaanxi, China, flowing north from the Qinling Mountains west of Xi'an. King Wen of Zhou built his capital Feng on its west bank, and his son King Wu built Hao on the east bank; together the two cities formed the…

frederic-thesiger-2nd-baron-chelmsford.s: Frederic Thesiger, 2nd Baron Chelmsford, was a British general who commanded the invasion of Zululand in the Anglo-Zulu War of 1879. His divided columns suffered the disaster at Isandlwana in January, but he restored his reputation in part by defeating the Zulu army at Ulundi…

francis-farewell.s: Francis Farewell was a former British naval officer who in 1824 led a small party of traders from the Cape to Port Natal, founding the settlement that became Durban. He visited Shaka, who granted the traders land around the bay, and he traded for ivory with the Zulu court.

famenne.s: The Famenne is a natural region of southern Belgium, a lowland depression of shale soils lying between the Condroz and the Ardennes in the provinces of Namur and Luxembourg. Its main town is Marche-en-Famenne.

ferrara.s: Ferrara is a city of Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy, near the Po. From the 13th century it was ruled by the House of Este, whose court made it a centre of Renaissance art, music and letters, home to the poets Ariosto and Tasso.

francesco-caracciolo.s: Francesco Caracciolo was a Neapolitan admiral who commanded the navy of the Parthenopean Republic in 1799. Having served the Bourbon king, he joined the republic and fought royalist and British ships in the Bay of Naples.

first-national-congress-of-chile.s: The First National Congress of Chile met in Santiago from July to December 1811, convened by the governing junta that had taken power in September 1810. The first representative assembly in Chilean history, it passed measures such as the freedom of wombs, which freed children…

felipe-santiago-salaverry.s: Felipe Santiago Salaverry was a Peruvian general who seized power in 1835 and ruled as Supreme Chief of Peru. He resisted the intervention of the Bolivian president Andrés de Santa Cruz, who had come to the aid of Luis José de Orbegoso.

fletcher-christian.s: Fletcher Christian was an English sailor, master's mate of HMS Bounty, who led the mutiny against Captain William Bligh in the South Pacific in April 1789. After setting Bligh adrift, he took the ship with eight other mutineers and a group of Tahitian men and women to…

flec.n: Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda
flec.s: The Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda (FLEC) is a separatist movement seeking independence for Cabinda, the oil-rich Angolan exclave north of the Congo River. Founded in 1963 from earlier Cabindan movements, it claimed independence in 1975 but was excluded…

fretilin.s: Fretilin, the Revolutionary Front for an Independent East Timor, was founded in 1974 after the Carnation Revolution in Portugal. It won a brief civil war in 1975 and declared independence on 28 November, nine days before Indonesia invaded.

fussen.s: Füssen is a town on the Lech at the foot of the Alps in Bavaria, Germany. It belonged to the prince-bishops of Augsburg, who kept a summer residence in its High Castle, and it lay on the old road to Italy.

francois-fenelon.s: François Fénelon was a French archbishop, theologian and writer. As tutor to Louis XIV's grandson, the Duke of Burgundy, he wrote The Adventures of Telemachus, whose criticism of absolute monarchy angered the king.

furstenwalde.s: Fürstenwalde is a town on the Spree in Brandenburg, Germany, east of Berlin. From the late 14th century it was the seat of the bishops of Lebus, whose cathedral of St Mary survives, until the bishopric was secularised after the Reformation.

friedrich-von-wangen.s: Friedrich von Wangen was prince-bishop of Trent from 1207 to 1218 and an imperial official in Italy. He strengthened the bishops' rule over their principality and had their rights recorded in the Codex Wangianus.

frombork.s: Frombork (German Frauenburg) is a small town in northern Poland on the Vistula Lagoon. From the 13th century it was the seat of the cathedral chapter of Warmia, whose fortified Gothic cathedral stands on a hill above the town.

fan-noli.s: Fan Noli was an Albanian Orthodox bishop, writer and politician. In the United States he founded an independent Albanian Orthodox church and became its bishop.

fruitbearing-society.s: The Fruitbearing Society (Fruchtbringende Gesellschaft) was a learned society founded at Weimar in 1617 by Prince Ludwig of Anhalt-Köthen and others to cultivate and purify the German language. Modelled on the Italian Accademia della Crusca, it had its seat at Köthen for many…

fayzabad-badakhshan.s: Fayzabad is a town in north-eastern Afghanistan, the capital of Badakhshan province, on the Kokcha river in the foothills of the Hindu Kush. From the 17th century it was the seat of the mirs who ruled Badakhshan, and it has long been the main market of the province, on routes…

faizabad.s: Faizabad is a city in Uttar Pradesh, India, on the Ghaghara river beside Ayodhya. It grew in the 1730s as the residence of the early nawabs of Awadh, Saadat Ali Khan and Safdar Jang, and was the capital of Awadh until Asaf-ud-Daula moved his court to Lucknow in 1775.

fyodor-romanovich-of-beloozero.s: Fyodor Romanovich was a prince of Beloozero in northern Rus' in the 14th century. An ally of Grand Prince Dmitry Donskoy of Moscow, he fought in the coalition army against the Tatar commander Mamai and was killed with his son Ivan at the Battle of Kulikovo in 1380.

ferdinando-ii-de-medici.s: Ferdinando II de' Medici was Grand Duke of Tuscany from 1621 to 1670. His long reign saw plague, economic decline and the indecisive War of Castro against the Barberini.

ferdinand-of-brunswick-wolfenbuttel.s: Ferdinand of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel was a Prussian field marshal and one of Frederick the Great's best generals. In the Seven Years' War he commanded the allied army of Britain, Hanover, Brunswick and Hesse-Kassel in western Germany from 1757, driving the French back across…

frederic-maurice-de-la-tour-dauvergne.n: Frédéric Maurice de La Tour d'Auvergne
frederic-maurice-de-la-tour-dauvergne.s: Frédéric Maurice de La Tour d'Auvergne, Duke of Bouillon and Prince of Sedan, was the elder brother of Marshal Turenne. He repeatedly conspired against Cardinal Richelieu, and after joining the Cinq-Mars plot in 1642 he saved his life by surrendering Sedan to the French crown.

ferdinand-i-of-naples.s: Ferdinand I, known as Ferrante, was King of Naples from 1458 to 1494, the illegitimate son of Alfonso V of Aragon. He defeated a baronial revolt backed by the Angevin claimant early in his reign and crushed the Conspiracy of the Barons in 1485 to 1486.

ferdinando-gorges.s: Sir Ferdinando Gorges was an English soldier and colonial promoter, long governor of the fort at Plymouth, who backed English settlement in New England for decades. A leading member of the Plymouth Company and the Council for New England, he received a grant with John Mason in…

frog-lake-massacre.s: The Frog Lake massacre took place on 2 April 1885 at Frog Lake in present-day Alberta, during the North-West Resistance. Cree warriors of Big Bear's band, led by the war chief Wandering Spirit, killed nine people, including the Indian agent Thomas Quinn and two Catholic priests.

frederick-middleton.s: Sir Frederick Middleton was a British army officer who commanded the Canadian militia from 1884 to 1890. He led the North-West Field Force against the Métis and Cree in 1885, winning the Battle of Batoche in May and receiving Louis Riel's surrender.

foraker-act.s: The Foraker Act was a United States law of April 1900 that set up civil government in Puerto Rico after the Spanish–American War. It provided for a governor and executive council appointed by the US president and an elected house of delegates, but did not grant Puerto Ricans…

fengxiang.s: Fengxiang is a district of Baoji in western Shaanxi, China, on the plain north of the Wei River. Near it lay Yong, the capital and ritual centre of the State of Qin from 677 BCE, whose great tombs have been excavated nearby.

flag-of-denmark.s: The flag of Denmark, the Dannebrog, a white Scandinavian cross on a red field, is often said to be the oldest national flag in continuous use. Legend, first written down in the 16th century, says it fell from heaven during the Battle of Lindanise in Estonia in 1219, but the…

fraga.s: Fraga is a town in the province of Huesca in Aragon, north-eastern Spain, on the Cinca River. In the Middle Ages it was a Muslim stronghold where Alfonso I of Aragon suffered a fatal defeat in 1134, and it was finally taken by the Christians in 1149.

francisco-largo-caballero.s: Francisco Largo Caballero was a Spanish trade unionist and Socialist leader, head of the UGT union, whom admirers called 'the Spanish Lenin'. He was prime minister of the Second Republic from September 1936 to May 1937, bringing anarchist ministers into government, but fell…

federico-tinoco-granados.s: Federico Tinoco Granados was a Costa Rican army officer and war minister who overthrew President Alfredo González Flores in January 1917 and ruled as a dictator. The United States under Woodrow Wilson refused to recognise his government, and growing unrest and an invasion by…

fiesole.s: Fiesole is a hill town overlooking Florence in Tuscany, Italy. Founded by the Etruscans and later a Roman town, it was older than Florence and long its rival, until the Florentines conquered and destroyed it in 1125.

football-war.s: The Football War was a brief war between El Salvador and Honduras in July 1969, also called the Hundred Hours' War. Its causes were land disputes and the expulsion of Salvadoran migrants from Honduras, and it coincided with riots at World Cup qualifying matches between the two…

flying-gang.s: The Flying Gang was the name given to the pirates based at Nassau in the Bahamas between about 1716 and 1718, the period known as the Republic of Pirates. Its members included Benjamin Hornigold, Edward Teach (Blackbeard), Charles Vane, Sam Bellamy and Calico Jack.

fibonacci.s: Fibonacci, or Leonardo of Pisa, was an Italian mathematician who learned Arabic mathematics as a boy in Bugia (Béjaïa) in North Africa, where his father served as a Pisan customs official. His Liber Abaci of 1202 introduced the Hindu–Arabic numerals and their methods of…

f-w-de-klerk.s: F. W. de Klerk was the last state president of apartheid South Africa, serving from 1989 to 1994. In February 1990 he unbanned the African National Congress and other liberation movements and released Nelson Mandela, and he negotiated the end of white minority rule.

florida-parishes.s: The Florida Parishes are eight parishes of south-eastern Louisiana lying east of the Mississippi River and north of Lake Pontchartrain. Formerly part of Spanish West Florida, the area rebelled as the Republic of West Florida in 1810, was annexed by the United States the same…

fujiwara-clan.s: The Fujiwara clan was a Japanese aristocratic family descended from Nakatomi no Kamatari, who received the name Fujiwara in 669. By marrying daughters into the imperial line, its leaders dominated the court as regents (sesshō and kampaku) from the 9th to the 11th century,…

fort-ross.s: Fort Ross was a Russian settlement on the coast of northern California, north of San Francisco, founded by the Russian-American Company in 1812. It was meant to grow food for the Alaskan colonies and to hunt sea otters, but it never became profitable and was sold to John…

feurs.s: Feurs is a town on the Loire in the Loire department of central France. As Forum Segusiavorum it was the chief town of the Gallic Segusiavi under Roman rule, after the foundation of Lugdunum on their land.

fourviere.s: Fourvière is a hill in Lyon, France, overlooking the confluence of the Saône and Rhône. The Roman colony of Lugdunum was founded on it in 43 BCE, and the remains of its theatre and odeon survive on the slope.

first-seminole-war.s: The First Seminole War was a conflict of 1817 to 1818 in which American forces under Andrew Jackson invaded Spanish Florida against the Seminole and Black Seminoles. Jackson burned towns, seized the Spanish posts of St. Marks and Pensacola and executed two British traders.

fu-hao.s: Fu Hao was a consort of the Shang king Wu Ding who also led armies in the field, as oracle-bone inscriptions record. Her tomb at Anyang, found intact in 1976, held more than 400 bronze objects, over 700 jades and weapons bearing her name.

fashoda.s: Fashoda, now Kodok, is a town on the west bank of the White Nile in South Sudan. It was the royal centre of the Shilluk kingdom from about the 16th century.

farrukh-yasar.s: Farrukh Yasar was Shirvanshah from the 1460s until 1500, ruling from Shamakhi as an ally of the Aq Qoyunlu. In 1488, with Aq Qoyunlu help, his forces defeated and killed Shaykh Haydar, leader of the militant Safavid order, who had invaded Shirvan.

fourah-bay-college.s: Fourah Bay College is a college in Freetown, Sierra Leone, founded by the Church Missionary Society in 1827, the first Western-style institution of higher learning in West Africa. Affiliated with Durham University from 1876, it trained clergy, teachers and clerks for much of…

fort-mose.s: Fort Mose, or Gracia Real de Santa Teresa de Mose, was a fortified settlement north of St. Augustine in Spanish Florida, founded in 1738 for Africans who had escaped slavery in the British Carolinas and accepted Catholicism. Led by the militia captain Francisco Menéndez, it…

francis-drake.s: Francis Drake (c. 1540–1596) was an English sea captain and privateer who raided Spain's American empire. He completed the second circumnavigation of the world between 1577 and 1580, was knighted by Elizabeth I, and was vice-admiral in the fleet that defeated the Spanish…

funcinpec.s: FUNCINPEC is a Cambodian royalist party founded by Prince Norodom Sihanouk in 1981 as a resistance movement against the Vietnamese-backed government. Its French acronym stands for National United Front for an Independent, Neutral, Peaceful and Cooperative Cambodia.

fen-river.s: The Fen River is the second-largest tributary of the Yellow River and the longest river of Shanxi province, China, flowing about 700 kilometres south through Taiyuan to join the Yellow River. Its fertile valley in southern Shanxi was the homeland of the State of Jin, whose…

fort-san-marcos-de-apalache.s: Fort San Marcos de Apalache was a Spanish fort at the junction of the Wakulla and St. Marks rivers in northern Florida, first built in 1679 to protect the Apalachee missions and their port. Rebuilt several times, it was held by the British from 1763 to 1783 and briefly…

fifa-world-cup.s: The FIFA World Cup is the international association football championship for men's national teams, organised every four years by FIFA since the first tournament in Uruguay in 1930, except in 1942 and 1946. It is the most widely watched sporting event in the world.

fan-li.s: Fan Li was a minister of King Goujian of Yue in the 5th century BCE who helped him rebuild Yue and destroy the State of Wu in 473 BCE. Doubting that Goujian would share his success, he then left the court and, according to the Shiji, grew rich as a merchant at Tao under the…

foureau-lamy-mission.s: The Foureau–Lamy Mission was a French military and scientific expedition of 1898–1900 led by the explorer Fernand Foureau and Commandant François Lamy. Crossing the Sahara from Algeria by way of Aïr and Zinder, it joined other French columns near Lake Chad and defeated Rabih…

fadl-ibn-ali.s: Fadl ibn Ali al-Abdali was the founder of the independent Sultanate of Lahej in southern Arabia, ruling from about 1728 to 1742. Leading the Abdali tribe, he threw off the authority of the Zaydi imams of the Qasimid State in Yemen and took control of Lahej and the port of…

fakr-ad-din-mosque.s: The Fakr ad-Din Mosque is a mosque in Mogadishu, Somalia, built in 1269 according to its foundation inscription. Built of coral stone and decorated with marble, it is one of the oldest surviving mosques in East Africa and reflects the wealth of Mogadishu as a trading city in…

fomboni.s: Fomboni is the main town of Moheli (Mwali), the smallest of the main islands of the Comoros. It was the seat of the sultans of Moheli in the 19th century, including Ramanetaka and Djoumbe Fatima, and its court life was shaped by Islam and Swahili culture.

fante.s: The Fante are an Akan people of the central coast of Ghana, around Cape Coast, Anomabu and Mankessim. From the 17th century their states grew rich as middlemen in the Atlantic trade in gold and slaves with European forts.

federal-treaty.s: The Federal Treaty was the constitution of the Swiss Confederation from 1815 to 1848, sworn on 7 August 1815 after the fall of Napoleon. It bound twenty-two sovereign cantons, including the newly admitted Geneva, Valais and Neuchâtel, in a loose alliance with a common Diet and…

fountain-of-arethusa.s: The Fountain of Arethusa is a freshwater spring on the island of Ortygia in Syracuse, Sicily, rising a few metres from the sea. Greek myth told that the nymph Arethusa, fleeing the river god Alpheus, was turned into a spring that flowed under the sea from Greece to Syracuse.

faro.s: Faro is a city on the south coast of Portugal, capital of the Algarve. As Roman Ossonoba it was an important port and later a bishopric; under Muslim rule it was known as Santa María de Harun, after the family that held it as a taifa in the 11th century.

fiame-mataafa-faumuina-mulinuu-ii.s: Fiamē Mataʻafa Faumuina Mulinuʻu II was a Samoan paramount chief and the first prime minister of Western Samoa. He led the government from 1959, guided the country to independence from New Zealand in 1962, and served until 1970 and again from 1973 until his death in 1975.

fritigern.s: Fritigern was a leader of the Thervingi Goths in the 370s. In 376, fleeing the Huns, his followers were admitted across the Danube into the Roman Empire, but abuse by Roman officials drove them to revolt.

fort-de-la-roche.s: Fort de la Roche was a stronghold built around 1640 by the Huguenot engineer Jean Le Vasseur on a rock above the harbour of Tortuga, off northern Hispaniola. Reached by an iron ladder and armed with cannon, it let the French hold the island against Spanish attack, repelling an…

fiji.s: Fiji is an island country in the south-western Pacific, made up of over 300 islands, chief among them Viti Levu and Vanua Levu, with its capital at Suva. Rival chiefdoms such as Bau dominated it until Seru Cakobau ceded the islands to Britain in 1874.

futuna-wallis-and-futuna.s: Futuna is a volcanic island in western Polynesia, part of the French overseas collectivity of Wallis and Futuna, together with the nearby uninhabited island of Alofi. It is divided between two traditional kingdoms, Sigave and Alo, whose kings are still recognised.

frascati.s: Frascati is a town in the Alban Hills about 20 kilometres south-east of Rome. It grew below the ancient city of Tusculum, and after Rome destroyed Tusculum in 1191 its refugees are said to have settled there.

fourth-universal.s: The Fourth Universal of the Central Rada was the proclamation, dated 22 January 1918, by which the Ukrainian People's Republic declared itself an independent and sovereign state. Issued in Kyiv as Bolshevik forces advanced on the city, it abandoned the Rada's earlier aim of…

francisco-jose-de-caldas.s: Francisco José de Caldas was a scientist from Popayán in New Granada, present-day Colombia. He took part in José Celestino Mutis's Royal Botanical Expedition, directed the astronomical observatory of Bogotá and devised a method of measuring altitude by the boiling point of water.

fuvahmulah.s: Fuvahmulah is a single-island atoll in the far south of the Maldives, between Huvadhu and Addu atolls, unusual for its freshwater lakes and the absence of a lagoon. In 1959 it joined Addu and Huvadhu in the breakaway United Suvadive Republic, which the Maldivian government…

fife.s: Fife is a council area and historic county of eastern Scotland, a peninsula between the Firth of Tay and the Firth of Forth. It takes its name from the Pictish province of Fib and was held by the powerful earls of Fife in the Middle Ages.

fors-de-bearn.s: The Fors de Béarn were the customary laws and liberties of the viscounty of Béarn in south-western France, written down from the 12th century and gathered into a general code in the 13th and 14th centuries. Each new viscount had to swear to uphold them before his subjects took…

fiora-river.s: The Fiora is a river of central Italy, about 80 km long, rising on Monte Amiata in Tuscany and flowing south through northern Lazio to the Tyrrhenian Sea near Montalto di Castro. The Etruscan city of Vulci stood on a plateau above it, and its valley was a route between the…

francois-tomb.s: The François Tomb is an Etruscan chamber tomb at Vulci, discovered in 1857 by Alessandro François, with wall paintings of the 4th century BCE. Its frescoes pair Achilles sacrificing Trojan prisoners with local heroes: Macstrna freeing Caelius Vibenna and Vulcian warriors…

fort-miamis.s: Fort Miamis was a British fort built in 1794 on the Maumee River, in present-day Maumee, Ohio, on territory claimed by the United States. After the Battle of Fallen Timbers in August 1794, its commander refused to open the gates to the retreating warriors of the Western…

fengjing.s: Fengjing, or Feng, was a capital of the Western Zhou dynasty on the west bank of the Feng River, south-west of present-day Xi'an. It was founded by King Wen of Zhou shortly before the conquest of the Shang.

frederick-stanley-arnot.s: Frederick Stanley Arnot (1858–1914) was a Scottish missionary of the Plymouth Brethren who travelled widely in south-central Africa. In 1886 he settled at Bunkeya, the capital of Msiri's Yeke kingdom in Katanga, where he founded the Garenganze mission.

fusagasuga.s: Fusagasugá is a city in the department of Cundinamarca, Colombia, south-west of Bogotá on the slopes of the Andes. Before the Spanish conquest it was a chiefdom of the Sutagao people on the edge of Muisca territory, conquered in the late fifteenth century by Saguamanchica,…

final-war-of-the-roman-republic.n: Final War of the Roman Republic
final-war-of-the-roman-republic.s: The Final War of the Roman Republic was the civil war of 32–30 BCE between Octavian and the alliance of Mark Antony and Cleopatra VII of Egypt. Octavian's fleet under Agrippa won the decisive Battle of Actium in 31 BCE, and Antony and Cleopatra took their own lives at…

french-conquest-of-algeria.s: The French conquest of Algeria began with the capture of Algiers from its Ottoman-era regency in 1830 and continued for decades. fourth-syrian-war.s: The Fourth Syrian War (219–217 BCE) was fought between the Seleucid king Antiochus III and Ptolemy IV of Egypt for control of Coele-Syria. Antiochus overran much of Phoenicia and Palestine, but Ptolemy's army, strengthened with native Egyptian troops, defeated him at Raphia in…

franco-turkish-war.s: The Franco-Turkish War (1918–1921), also called the Cilicia campaign, was fought between France, which occupied Cilicia after the First World War, and the Turkish nationalist forces led by Mustafa Kemal. Turkish resistance at Marash, Urfa and Aintab wore down the French…

first-war-of-scottish-independence.s: The First War of Scottish Independence was fought between Scotland and England from Edward I's invasion in 1296 to the Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton in 1328. Led by William Wallace and later Robert the Bruce, who won at Stirling Bridge (1297) and Bannockburn (1314), the…

franco-flemish-war-1297-1305.s: The Franco-Flemish War was fought from 1297 to 1305 between Philip IV of France and Guy of Dampierre, Count of Flanders. France occupied Flanders, but the Flemish towns revolted and defeated the French knights at the Battle of the Golden Spurs at Courtrai in 1302; after the…

first-peloponnesian-war.s: The First Peloponnesian War was fought from about 460 to 445 BCE between Athens and its allies and the Peloponnesian League led by Sparta, together with Corinth and Thebes. Athens controlled Boeotia for a time after its victory at Oenophyta (457 BCE) but lost it at Coronea in…

first-silesian-war.s: The First Silesian War was fought from 1740 to 1742 between Prussia under Frederick II and Habsburg Austria under Maria Theresa. Frederick invaded Silesia in December 1740, won at Mollwitz (1741) and Chotusitz (1742), and gained most of the province by the Treaty of Breslau,…

first-serbian-uprising.s: The First Serbian Uprising was the revolt of the Serbs of the Sanjak of Smederevo against Ottoman rule from 1804 to 1813. Begun against the oppressive Janissary commanders, the dahijas, it grew under Karađorđe Petrović into a war for independence and set up a Serbian…

free-state-basotho-wars.s: The Free State–Basotho Wars were a series of wars between the Orange Free State and the Basotho kingdom of Moshoeshoe I, fought in 1858 and from 1865 to 1868 over the fertile lands west of the Caledon River. The Boers took much Basotho farmland, and Moshoeshoe sought British…

franco-spanish-war-1635-1659.s: The Franco-Spanish War was fought from 1635 to 1659 between France and Habsburg Spain. It began when France under Cardinal Richelieu entered the Thirty Years' War, continued after the Peace of Westphalia, and was ended by the Treaty of the Pyrenees (1659), which gave France…

first-italian-war-of-independence.s: The First Italian War of Independence was fought in 1848–1849 by the Kingdom of Sardinia under Charles Albert, with volunteers from other Italian states, against the Austrian Empire. Begun amid the revolutions of 1848, it ended in Sardinian defeats at Custoza (1848) and Novara…

first-english-civil-war.s: The First English Civil War was fought from 1642 to 1646 between the Royalist supporters of King Charles I and the Parliamentarians. After indecisive early battles such as Edgehill, Parliament gained the upper hand at Marston Moor (1644) and, with the New Model Army, at Naseby…

franco-syrian-war.s: The Franco-Syrian War was a short conflict in 1920 between France and the Arab Kingdom of Syria proclaimed under Faisal I. When Faisal's government rejected the French mandate awarded at San Remo, French forces advanced from Lebanon, defeated a small Syrian army at Maysalun on…

first-mongol-invasion-of-burma.s: The First Mongol invasion of Burma was the series of campaigns from 1277 to 1287 by the Yuan dynasty of Kublai Khan against the Pagan Kingdom. After a battle at Ngasaunggyan (1277) and further invasions, Mongol forces reached the Pagan heartland in 1287; the kingdom broke…

first-jewish-roman-war.s: The First Jewish–Roman War was the revolt of the Jews of Judaea against Roman rule from 66 to 73 CE. Vespasian and then his son Titus reconquered the province; Jerusalem fell after a long siege in 70 CE and the Second Temple was destroyed, and the fortress of Masada was taken…

first-mongol-invasion-of-poland.s: The first Mongol invasion of Poland was a raid by a Mongol army under Baidar and Orda in 1240–1241, covering the flank of the main invasion of Hungary. The Mongols sacked Sandomierz and Kraków and on 9 April 1241 defeated the Silesian duke Henry II the Pious at Legnica, where…

french-invasion-of-switzerland.s: The French invasion of Switzerland took place in early 1798, when armies of the French Republic overran the Old Swiss Confederacy during the French Revolutionary Wars. Bern was defeated at Grauholz and fell in March 1798, and resistance in central Switzerland was crushed.

franco-moroccan-war.s: The Franco-Moroccan War was fought in 1844 between France and the Sultanate of Morocco, which had given refuge and support to the Algerian resistance leader Abd al-Qadir. A French fleet bombarded Tangier and Mogador, and Marshal Bugeaud defeated the Moroccan army at the Battle…

federal-war.s: The Federal War was a civil war in Venezuela from 1859 to 1863 between the Conservatives and the Liberals, who demanded a federal system. Federalist leaders such as Ezequiel Zamora and Juan Crisóstomo Falcón fought a largely guerrilla war in which many thousands died.

franco-savoyard-war-1600-1601.s: The Franco-Savoyard War of 1600–1601 was fought between Henry IV of France and Charles Emmanuel I, Duke of Savoy, over the Marquisate of Saluzzo, which Savoy had seized in 1588. French armies quickly overran Bresse and Savoy.

frankish-civil-war-715-718.s: The Frankish Civil War of 715–718 was a struggle for power after the death of the mayor of the palace Pepin of Herstal. Charles Martel, his illegitimate son, fought Pepin's widow Plectrude, the Neustrians under Ragenfrid and King Chilperic II.

french-conquest-of-corsica.s: The French conquest of Corsica followed the Treaty of Versailles of 1768, by which Genoa ceded its rights over the island to France. The Corsican Republic of Pasquale Paoli resisted, but was defeated at Ponte Novu in May 1769, and Paoli went into exile in Britain.

finnish-war.s: The Finnish War was fought from 1808 to 1809 between Sweden and the Russian Empire, which invaded Finland after Sweden refused to join Napoleon's Continental System. Russian forces took the fortress of Sveaborg and overran Finland.

flora-tristan.s: Flora Tristan was a French-Peruvian writer and socialist activist who argued that the progress of women's rights was bound up with the progress of the working class. Her account of a journey to Peru in 1833–1834, Peregrinations of a Pariah, appeared in 1838.

friedrich-schlegel.s: Friedrich Schlegel was a German literary critic, philosopher and Indologist who was, with his brother August Wilhelm, one of the main figures of Jena Romanticism. The brothers founded the journal Athenaeum, whose fragments and essays stated the principles of the Romantic…

frederic-chopin.s: Frédéric Chopin was a Polish composer and virtuoso pianist of the early Romantic period who wrote primarily for solo piano. Raised in Warsaw, he left Poland less than a month before the November Uprising of 1830 broke out and settled in Paris in 1831, never to return.

fifth-pan-african-congress.s: The Fifth Pan-African Congress was a meeting of the Pan-African movement held at Chorlton-on-Medlock Town Hall in Manchester, England, from 15 to 21 October 1945.
